# 넷리스트 기반 High-Speed IO 개념도 그리기 — 회귀 시험 세트 묶음

> **Release R0.1** — 명세서 v6.1 — 소스 커밋 `bdcf300` — 2026-11-16

`tests/regression/`의 시험 netlist·정답지·설계 메모 전부. 쓰는 법은 그 안의 `README.md`. **정답지·설계 메모·name_map은 검증 쪽에만 준다(그리는 쪽에는 netlist.sp만).**

## 복원 방법

`python3 restore.py HSIO_R0.1_TESTS.md netlist-hsio-concept-diagram` → 모든 줄 `OK`, 마지막 줄 `0 checksum mismatches`.

### 복원 스크립트 (restore.py)

`````python
import hashlib, os, re, sys
src = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read()
dest = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "netlist-hsio-concept-diagram"
pat = re.compile(r"^### FILE: (\S+)\n<!-- sha256=([0-9a-f]{64}) newline=([01]) -->\n`{5}\w*\n(.*?)\n`{5}$", re.S | re.M)
n = bad = 0
for path, sha, nl, body in pat.findall(src):
    data = body + ("\n" if nl == "1" else "")
    full = os.path.join(dest, path)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(full) or ".", exist_ok=True)
    with open(full, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as f:
        f.write(data)
    ok = hashlib.sha256(data.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest() == sha
    bad += not ok
    n += 1
    print(("OK   " if ok else "BAD  ") + path)
print("%d files restored, %d checksum mismatches" % (n, bad))
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
`````

# 회귀 시험 세트

명세서(`DRAWING_PLAN.md`)나 도구를 고친 뒤 다시 돌려, 전에 맞던 것이 틀려지지 않았는지 보는 시험 netlist 모음이다.
모두 시험용으로 만든 가상 회로다(실제 사내 설계 아님). 루프 1–4회차에서 쓴 것과 같다.

## 쓰는 법 (반드시 지킬 것)

- **그리는 쪽(AGENT 2 / GLM)에게는 `netlist.sp`만 준다.** 파일 이름도 중립적으로 바꿔 준다(예: `netlist_x.sp`).
- **`answer_key.json`, `answer_key_README.md`, `intent.md`, `name_map.json`은 검증 쪽(AGENT 3)에게만** 준다. 그리는 쪽으로 가는 수정 요청(`fix_request.md`)에는 이 내용을 넣지 않는다(명세서 §4.3).
- 정답지 분류 이름은 명세서 부록 B로 명세서 분류에 맞춰 대조한다. 정답지와 일부러 다르게 정한 정책(정적 slew·CTLE 코드, 공통모드, 루프가 만든 아날로그 트림 — 명세서 부록 C.8 V7·V14·V15)은 불일치로 세지 않는다.
- 판정은 두 축: 그림(그린 쪽 원인 불통과 0) / 명세(명세서 원인 불통과 0).

- 기준 결과(RX AFE)는 이 세트가 아니라 `reference/rx_afe/`에 있다(정답 그림까지 있음).
- 이름 가림 시험(`t4_nameblind`): 같은 그리는 절차를 `t3_nand_io`와 `t4_nameblind`에 각각 돌린 뒤, `name_map.json`으로 분류·블록 역할을 맞대어 본다(체크리스트 N1). 이름 있는 판과 가림판이 다르면 명세서가 이름에 기대고 있다는 신호다.
- 실업무 netlist에서 새 문제가 나오면, 사용자가 확인한 `annotations.json`을 그 netlist의 정답지로 올려 이 세트에 더할 수 있다(사내에만 보관).

### FILE: tests/regression/t1_dcc/intent.md
<!-- sha256=28fe7c285af0baf976e764c3215415ada9fcb1ebb4be18aa5593d74bd72947cc newline=1 -->
`````markdown
# Design intent notes

Process assumed: generic 28 nm-class CMOS, core devices `nch`, `pch`, `nch_lvt` (models come from the PDK, not included). Nominal vdd = vddq = 0.9 V.

## tx.sp: 4:1 SST serial-link transmitter with 3-tap FFE

**Top cell:** `tx_top`

- **High-speed data in:** `din<3:0>`: quarter-rate parallel data, sent with `din<0>` first. It is launched by the digital logic on `clk_div4` and sampled inside on the falling edge of ck4.
- **High-speed data out:** `txp` / `txn`, the differential pads (SST voltage-mode, about 50 ohm per side with all segments on and mid-range zcal).
- **Clock in:** `ckhr_p` / `ckhr_n`, the half-rate differential CML clock from the PLL.
- **Clock out:** `clk_div4`, the quarter-rate CMOS clock sent to the digital parallel interface.
- **Digital control:**
  - `oe`: output enable. When 0, all driver slices go hi-Z.
  - `eidle`: electrical idle. All slices go hi-Z and the 2k/2k common-mode keeper is switched onto each pad.
  - `en_main<3:0>`: enables for the binary-weighted main-tap slices (1/2/4/8 units). Sets the main strength and swing.
  - `sel_pre<1:0>`: steers pre-cursor slice groups of 1 and 2 units from main data (0) to inverted next-bit data (1). Sets the pre-tap weight, 0 to 3 out of 25 units.
  - `sel_post<2:0>`: steers post-cursor slice groups of 1, 2 and 4 units from main data to inverted previous-bit data. Sets the post-tap weight, 0 to 7 out of 25 units.
  - `zcal_p<1:0>` / `zcal_n<1:0>`: impedance-calibration fingers (weights 1x and 2x) in every slice, for the pull-up and pull-down legs separately.
  - `bias_en`: enables the bias. When 0, `nbias` is pulled low and the clock receiver turns off.
- **Bias:** `ibias_50u`, a 50 uA reference current sunk into a diode-connected NMOS. It is mirrored to the CML clock buffer (x8, 400 uA) and to the CML-to-CMOS tails (x2).
- **Power:** `vdd` (core logic, clock path, tap muxes), `vddq` (pre-drivers, SST slices, pad ESD), `vss`.

**Sub-blocks**

- `tx_bias`: turns the reference current into the `nbias` voltage, with a power-down pull-down and a decap.
- `tx_clkrx`: 100 ohm differential input termination (50 + 50 ohm to an AC-grounded common-mode node), a resistively loaded CML clock buffer, and two `cml2cmos` cells with swapped inputs. Outputs `ck2` / `ck2b`.
- `cml2cmos`: 5T NMOS-input OTA followed by two inverters (non-inverting).
- `dff` (instance xi2 in the top cell): divide-by-2 with `qb` fed back to `d`. Turns `ck2` into `ck4` / `ck4b`.
- `tx_ffe_tapgen`: 9 DFFs clocked on the falling edge of ck4. Builds three time-aligned 4-bit words:
  - main = the input word delayed by one word;
  - pre = main advanced by 1 UI;
  - post = main delayed by 1 UI.
- `ser4to1` (x3: main, pre, post): 2-level tree of `mux2to1` cells (ck4 stage, then ck2 stage). Produces complementary full-rate outputs. A tgate in the outb path matches its delay to the extra inverter in the out path.
- `mux2to1`: two DFFs plus a half-cycle latch on the d1 path, then a clocked tristate-inverter selector.
- `dff` / `dlatch`: master-slave flop built from C2MOS-style latches.
- `tx_ctrl_dec`: static gates that produce:
  - the internal enable `en_t = oe & !eidle`;
  - per-bit main enables gated with `en_t`;
  - complements of the select and zcal_n codes;
  - keeper controls.
- `tx_drv_pad` (x2, one per pad). Each contains:
  - `tx_tapmux` per slice group, including a dummy mux on the main path for delay matching;
  - a `tx_predrv` tapered inverter chain per group;
  - binary-weighted `sst_slice` instances, 25 units in total;
  - the idle common-mode keeper;
  - a 10 ohm CDM series resistor;
  - `tx_pad_esd`.

  The negative FFE taps come from feeding the opposite polarity of pre/post data into each pad.
- `sst_slice`: unit SST leg. NAND/NOR gating gives data, enable and hi-Z control. The pull-up and pull-down stacks each have a base finger plus two zcal fingers, and their own 900 ohm series resistor.
- `tx_pad_esd`: GGNMOS to vss and gate-tied PMOS to vddq (with gate resistors), plus 120 fF pad parasitic.
- `esd_rc_clamp` (on vddq and on vdd): RC-triggered big-NMOS rail clamp.
- Top-level MOS decaps.

## dcc.sp: digitally controlled duty-cycle corrector (differential clock)

**Top cell:** `dcc_top`

- **Clock in:** `clkin_p` / `clkin_n`, a differential CML clock from the distribution network.
- **Clock out:** `clkout_p` / `clkout_n`, the duty-corrected CMOS clocks.
- **Detector clock:** `cmp_clk`, a slow comparator clock (for example tens of MHz) from the DCC controller.
- **Detector out:** `dcd_out` / `dcd_outb`. `dcd_out = 1` when avg(clkout_p) > avg(clkout_n), meaning the p duty is above 50% (with `dcd_swap = 0`). The FSM that turns this into codes is off-block.
- **Digital control:**
  - `clk_en`: enables the bias and receivers. When 0, the receiver outputs are forced high.
  - `dcc_en`: correction enable. When 0, all trim legs are off and the clock passes through.
  - `dcc_sign`: correction direction. 1 increases the clkout_p duty and decreases the clkout_n duty; 0 does the reverse.
  - `dcc_mag<4:0>`: binary correction magnitude, 0 to 31 unit legs.
  - `dcd_en`: gates the comparator clock.
  - `dcd_swap`: chopper. Swaps the comparator inputs to cancel offset; the controller inverts `dcd_out` when it is set.
- **Bias:** `ibias_25u`, a 25 uA reference mirrored x4 into each CML-to-CMOS receiver tail.
- **Power:** `vdd`, `vss`.

**Sub-blocks**

- `dcc_bias`: diode-connected reference with a power-down pull-down and a decap.
- `cml2cmos_rx` (x2, with swapped inputs for p and n): 5T OTA plus two inverters, with a PMOS pull-up that sets a defined state when disabled.
- `dcc_code_dec`: NAND3 + inverter decode into four control buses:
  - `a = en & sign & mag`, and its complement `ab`;
  - `b = en & !sign & mag`, and its complement `bb`.
- `dcc_path` (x2): `dcc_adj_stage` followed by a 2/6/16x inverter buffer chain (4 inversions, non-inverting overall), with a fixed MOS-cap load on the adjust node.
  - p path: PU legs are driven by `b`, PD legs by `a`.
  - n path: PU legs by `a`, PD legs by `b`.

  Stronger PD in the adjust stage gives a higher output duty, and stronger PU gives a lower output duty.
- `dcc_adj_stage`: inverting stage made of a base inverter in parallel with binary-weighted (1/2/4/8/16) `dcc_adj_leg` instances.
- `dcc_adj_leg`: unit leg with a series PMOS switch on the PU side and a series NMOS switch on the PD side, each enabled independently.
- `dcd`: duty-cycle detector. It contains:
  - two `rc_lpf` second-order RC averagers (200k / 0.5p, 200k / 1p);
  - the `dcd_swap` chopper, built from `dcc_tgate` cells;
  - an AND clock gate made of transistors;
  - an `sa_comp` StrongARM comparator with an `nch_lvt` input pair and a NAND SR latch (`dcc_nand2`).
- `dcc_decap`: MOS decap cell (x2 at the top level).
`````

### FILE: tests/regression/t1_tx/intent.md
<!-- sha256=28fe7c285af0baf976e764c3215415ada9fcb1ebb4be18aa5593d74bd72947cc newline=1 -->
`````markdown
# Design intent notes

Process assumed: generic 28 nm-class CMOS, core devices `nch`, `pch`, `nch_lvt` (models come from the PDK, not included). Nominal vdd = vddq = 0.9 V.

## tx.sp: 4:1 SST serial-link transmitter with 3-tap FFE

**Top cell:** `tx_top`

- **High-speed data in:** `din<3:0>`: quarter-rate parallel data, sent with `din<0>` first. It is launched by the digital logic on `clk_div4` and sampled inside on the falling edge of ck4.
- **High-speed data out:** `txp` / `txn`, the differential pads (SST voltage-mode, about 50 ohm per side with all segments on and mid-range zcal).
- **Clock in:** `ckhr_p` / `ckhr_n`, the half-rate differential CML clock from the PLL.
- **Clock out:** `clk_div4`, the quarter-rate CMOS clock sent to the digital parallel interface.
- **Digital control:**
  - `oe`: output enable. When 0, all driver slices go hi-Z.
  - `eidle`: electrical idle. All slices go hi-Z and the 2k/2k common-mode keeper is switched onto each pad.
  - `en_main<3:0>`: enables for the binary-weighted main-tap slices (1/2/4/8 units). Sets the main strength and swing.
  - `sel_pre<1:0>`: steers pre-cursor slice groups of 1 and 2 units from main data (0) to inverted next-bit data (1). Sets the pre-tap weight, 0 to 3 out of 25 units.
  - `sel_post<2:0>`: steers post-cursor slice groups of 1, 2 and 4 units from main data to inverted previous-bit data. Sets the post-tap weight, 0 to 7 out of 25 units.
  - `zcal_p<1:0>` / `zcal_n<1:0>`: impedance-calibration fingers (weights 1x and 2x) in every slice, for the pull-up and pull-down legs separately.
  - `bias_en`: enables the bias. When 0, `nbias` is pulled low and the clock receiver turns off.
- **Bias:** `ibias_50u`, a 50 uA reference current sunk into a diode-connected NMOS. It is mirrored to the CML clock buffer (x8, 400 uA) and to the CML-to-CMOS tails (x2).
- **Power:** `vdd` (core logic, clock path, tap muxes), `vddq` (pre-drivers, SST slices, pad ESD), `vss`.

**Sub-blocks**

- `tx_bias`: turns the reference current into the `nbias` voltage, with a power-down pull-down and a decap.
- `tx_clkrx`: 100 ohm differential input termination (50 + 50 ohm to an AC-grounded common-mode node), a resistively loaded CML clock buffer, and two `cml2cmos` cells with swapped inputs. Outputs `ck2` / `ck2b`.
- `cml2cmos`: 5T NMOS-input OTA followed by two inverters (non-inverting).
- `dff` (instance xi2 in the top cell): divide-by-2 with `qb` fed back to `d`. Turns `ck2` into `ck4` / `ck4b`.
- `tx_ffe_tapgen`: 9 DFFs clocked on the falling edge of ck4. Builds three time-aligned 4-bit words:
  - main = the input word delayed by one word;
  - pre = main advanced by 1 UI;
  - post = main delayed by 1 UI.
- `ser4to1` (x3: main, pre, post): 2-level tree of `mux2to1` cells (ck4 stage, then ck2 stage). Produces complementary full-rate outputs. A tgate in the outb path matches its delay to the extra inverter in the out path.
- `mux2to1`: two DFFs plus a half-cycle latch on the d1 path, then a clocked tristate-inverter selector.
- `dff` / `dlatch`: master-slave flop built from C2MOS-style latches.
- `tx_ctrl_dec`: static gates that produce:
  - the internal enable `en_t = oe & !eidle`;
  - per-bit main enables gated with `en_t`;
  - complements of the select and zcal_n codes;
  - keeper controls.
- `tx_drv_pad` (x2, one per pad). Each contains:
  - `tx_tapmux` per slice group, including a dummy mux on the main path for delay matching;
  - a `tx_predrv` tapered inverter chain per group;
  - binary-weighted `sst_slice` instances, 25 units in total;
  - the idle common-mode keeper;
  - a 10 ohm CDM series resistor;
  - `tx_pad_esd`.

  The negative FFE taps come from feeding the opposite polarity of pre/post data into each pad.
- `sst_slice`: unit SST leg. NAND/NOR gating gives data, enable and hi-Z control. The pull-up and pull-down stacks each have a base finger plus two zcal fingers, and their own 900 ohm series resistor.
- `tx_pad_esd`: GGNMOS to vss and gate-tied PMOS to vddq (with gate resistors), plus 120 fF pad parasitic.
- `esd_rc_clamp` (on vddq and on vdd): RC-triggered big-NMOS rail clamp.
- Top-level MOS decaps.

## dcc.sp: digitally controlled duty-cycle corrector (differential clock)

**Top cell:** `dcc_top`

- **Clock in:** `clkin_p` / `clkin_n`, a differential CML clock from the distribution network.
- **Clock out:** `clkout_p` / `clkout_n`, the duty-corrected CMOS clocks.
- **Detector clock:** `cmp_clk`, a slow comparator clock (for example tens of MHz) from the DCC controller.
- **Detector out:** `dcd_out` / `dcd_outb`. `dcd_out = 1` when avg(clkout_p) > avg(clkout_n), meaning the p duty is above 50% (with `dcd_swap = 0`). The FSM that turns this into codes is off-block.
- **Digital control:**
  - `clk_en`: enables the bias and receivers. When 0, the receiver outputs are forced high.
  - `dcc_en`: correction enable. When 0, all trim legs are off and the clock passes through.
  - `dcc_sign`: correction direction. 1 increases the clkout_p duty and decreases the clkout_n duty; 0 does the reverse.
  - `dcc_mag<4:0>`: binary correction magnitude, 0 to 31 unit legs.
  - `dcd_en`: gates the comparator clock.
  - `dcd_swap`: chopper. Swaps the comparator inputs to cancel offset; the controller inverts `dcd_out` when it is set.
- **Bias:** `ibias_25u`, a 25 uA reference mirrored x4 into each CML-to-CMOS receiver tail.
- **Power:** `vdd`, `vss`.

**Sub-blocks**

- `dcc_bias`: diode-connected reference with a power-down pull-down and a decap.
- `cml2cmos_rx` (x2, with swapped inputs for p and n): 5T OTA plus two inverters, with a PMOS pull-up that sets a defined state when disabled.
- `dcc_code_dec`: NAND3 + inverter decode into four control buses:
  - `a = en & sign & mag`, and its complement `ab`;
  - `b = en & !sign & mag`, and its complement `bb`.
- `dcc_path` (x2): `dcc_adj_stage` followed by a 2/6/16x inverter buffer chain (4 inversions, non-inverting overall), with a fixed MOS-cap load on the adjust node.
  - p path: PU legs are driven by `b`, PD legs by `a`.
  - n path: PU legs by `a`, PD legs by `b`.

  Stronger PD in the adjust stage gives a higher output duty, and stronger PU gives a lower output duty.
- `dcc_adj_stage`: inverting stage made of a base inverter in parallel with binary-weighted (1/2/4/8/16) `dcc_adj_leg` instances.
- `dcc_adj_leg`: unit leg with a series PMOS switch on the PU side and a series NMOS switch on the PD side, each enabled independently.
- `dcd`: duty-cycle detector. It contains:
  - two `rc_lpf` second-order RC averagers (200k / 0.5p, 200k / 1p);
  - the `dcd_swap` chopper, built from `dcc_tgate` cells;
  - an AND clock gate made of transistors;
  - an `sa_comp` StrongARM comparator with an `nch_lvt` input pair and a NAND SR latch (`dcc_nand2`).
- `dcc_decap`: MOS decap cell (x2 at the top level).
`````

+ main<2> main<3> pre<0> pre<1> pre<2> pre<3> post<0> post<1> post<2>
+ post<3> vdd vss

xi2 din<2> ck ckb w1<2> net032 vdd vss dff
xi3 din<3> ck ckb w1<3> net033 vdd vss dff

xi7 w1<3> ck ckb pre<2> net037 vdd vss dff

** w2<0>=post<1>, w2<1>=post<2>, w2<2>=post<3>, w2<3>=pre<2>
** main bits are buffered copies of w2 (separate load from tap nets)

+ selb_post<2> znb<0> znb<1> keep_en keep_enb vdd vss

m4 enb_t oe vdd vdd pch l=30e-9 w=400e-9 m=1 nf=1

m9 en_t enb_t vss vss nch l=30e-9 w=400e-9 m=1 nf=1

m19 net062 en_t vss vss nch l=30e-9 w=400e-9 m=1 nf=1

m21 en_m<1> enb_m<1> vss vss nch l=30e-9 w=200e-9 m=1 nf=1

m27 en_m<2> enb_m<2> vss vss nch l=30e-9 w=200e-9 m=1 nf=1

m5 gpu1 en vddq vddq pch l=30e-9 w=300e-9 m=1 nf=1
m6 gpu1 zp0 vddq vddq pch l=30e-9 w=300e-9 m=1 nf=1

m8 net091 en net092 vss nch l=30e-9 w=400e-9 m=1 nf=1

m17 gpd0 enb net095 vddq pch l=30e-9 w=800e-9 m=1 nf=2

m19 gpd0 enb vss vss nch l=30e-9 w=200e-9 m=1 nf=1
m20 net096 d vddq vddq pch l=30e-9 w=900e-9 m=1 nf=2
m21 net097 enb net096 vddq pch l=30e-9 w=900e-9 m=1 nf=2
m22 gpd1 znb0 net097 vddq pch l=30e-9 w=900e-9 m=1 nf=2

m28 gpd2 znb1 net099 vddq pch l=30e-9 w=900e-9 m=1 nf=2

+ enb_m<1> enb_m<2> enb_m<3> en_t enb_t sel_pre<0> sel_pre<1> selb_pre<0>
+ selb_pre<1> sel_post<0> sel_post<1> sel_post<2> selb_post<0> selb_post<1>

xi0 dm dm vss vdd net0100 vdd vss tx_tapmux
xi1 net0100 dmain_pd vddq vss tx_predrv m=4

xi7 net0101 dpre_pd<0> vddq vss tx_predrv m=1

xi9 dm dpre sel_pre<1> selb_pre<1> net0102 vdd vss tx_tapmux

xi11 dpre_pd<1> en_t enb_t zp<0> zp<1> znb<0> znb<1> drv_out vddq vss sst_slice m=2
** post-cursor slices
xi12 dm dpost sel_post<0> selb_post<0> net0103 vdd vss tx_tapmux
xi13 net0103 dpost_pd<0> vddq vss tx_predrv m=1
xi14 dpost_pd<0> en_t enb_t zp<0> zp<1> znb<0> znb<1> drv_out vddq vss sst_slice m=1

### FILE: tests/regression/t2_bist/answer_key_README.md
<!-- sha256=28d00da03242c175398dfdcb87509629faa82a82f4bdcb62ff545fcea4148cc9 newline=1 -->
`````markdown
# Answer keys

There is one JSON file per netlist: `bist.json` (`../bist.sp`), `zqcal.json` (`../zqcal.sp`) and `dqs_rx.json` (`../dqs_rx.sp`). Each one is the ground truth for checking a block diagram drawn from that netlist.

**Top-level fields**
- `top`: the top cell.
- `supplies` / `grounds`: supply and ground net names.
- `ports`: one entry per top-level port. A bus is grouped as `name<msb:lsb>`. Each entry has a `class` (`hs_data_in`, `hs_data_out`, `clock_in`, `clock_out`, `important_control`, `general_control`, `bias`, `power`, `slow_signal` or `test_digital`) and a one-line `function`.

**`cells`**

The keys cover every cell that contains subcircuit instances, plus the leaf cells on the high-speed, clock or strobe path (and a few other notable leaf cells). Each cell has these fields:
- `role`: what the block is.
- `on_high_speed_path`: whether the block carries the high-speed data, clock or strobe.
- `inverting`: the polarity from main input to main output. `null` means it does not apply (logic or control blocks).
- `children`: the subcircuit instances only. Iterated instances are grouped, e.g. `xi0<3:0>`. Direct MOS, R and C devices are not listed as children. Their counts are appended at the end of `notes` as `[direct primitives in this cell: ...]`.
- `signal_flow`: rows of `[from, to, net, class]` in rough flow order.
  - `from` and `to` are written as `<inst>.<pin>`. `PORT.<pin>` means the cell's own port. In leaf cells, a device terminal is written as `mn0.g` (MOS d/g/s/b) or `r0.p` / `r0.n` (first / second node of an R or C).
  - `net` is the net name inside that cell.
  - `class` is one of `hs_data`, `word_data`, `clock`, `strobe`, `analog`, `reference`, `bias`, `control`, `code`, `decision`, `status`, `data` or `logic`.
  - For buses and repeated bit slices, only representative bits are listed (for example `<0>` and `<3>`). The other bits are wired the same way.
- `controls`: each control net or bus, and what it sets.
- `notes`: feedback loops, unused outputs, deliberate asymmetry and other things a reviewer needs to know.

Every `from`/`to` pair in `signal_flow` was checked by script against the netlist. Both ends resolve to the stated net.
`````

### FILE: tests/regression/t2_bist/intent.md
<!-- sha256=f10d339ce64990a4469ac36d7f167552ef1c739d4a201f49f1e86e4654eab048 newline=1 -->
`````markdown
# Designer intent notes

All three netlists are HSPICE (hspiceD-style) schematic exports. The top cell of each one is a `.subckt` that nothing else instantiates. Device models (`nch`, `pch`, `nch_lvt`, `pch_lvt`, `nch_18`, `pch_18`) come from the PDK and are not included. Every subcircuit is defined in its own file. Bus pins are written MSB first.

---

## 1. bist.sp: HSIO loopback BIST

**Top cell:** `hsio_bist_top`

**Supplies:** `vdd` = 0.9 V core (logic, clocks, samplers); `vddq` = 1.0 V (CML serializer output, TX driver, loopback mux, CTLE); `vss`.

**High-speed data**
- Out: `txp` / `txn`. These are the CML TX pads (50 Ohm back-terminated to vddq). The PRBS pattern leaves the chip here.
- In: `rxp` / `rxn`. These are the external RX pads (2x50 Ohm termination to a self-biased CM node of 0.7*vddq). The loopback mux selects them when `lpbk_en`=0.
- Internal loopback: the TX pads `txp/txn` are tapped through 200 Ohm series resistors into the second input of the loopback mux.

**Clock inputs:** `ckp` / `ckn` is the 4 GHz half-rate differential clock (8 Gb/s, DDR). From it the chip derives: ck/ckb (serializer final mux), wclk/wclkb = ck/2 (TX word clock, 4 bits/word), rck/rckb (RX sampling clock = ck through the delay trim), and rwclk/rwclkb = rck/2 (RX word clock).

**Control**
- `cfg<8:0>` + `cfg_wr` (rising edge writes) feed the mode register:
  - `cfg<8>` prbs_sel: 0 = PRBS7 (x^7+x^6+1), 1 = PRBS15 (x^15+x^14+1), for both the generator and the checker.
  - `cfg<7>` lpbk_en: 1 = internal TX→RX loopback, 0 = external rxp/rxn.
  - `cfg<6>` tx_en: enables the TX CML driver tail, and the generator runs only when it is set.
  - `cfg<5>` rx_en: CTLE tail enable.
  - `cfg<4>` chk_en: checker run enable.
  - `cfg<3>` err_inj: a 0→1 write injects a single bit error, by inverting tx_d<0> for one word.
  - `cfg<2:0>` rdly<2:0>: binary-weighted switched-cap delay trim of the RX sampling clock (rck/rckb) relative to the TX clock. This sets the sampling phase in loopback.
- `bist_start`, `bist_stop`: asynchronous level/edge requests, synchronized to wclk. Start sets RUN and clears the error counter and lock detector (clr_b pulse). Stop clears RUN and sets DONE.
- `rstb`: global active-low asynchronous reset. It also seeds the LFSR with 0...01.
- `bist_en`: bias enable.

**Bias:** `ibias` is a 100 uA reference current into the diode in `bist_bias`. It produces `vbn` for all CML tails: ser mux 1.6 mA, TX driver 8 mA, loopback mux 1.6 mA, CTLE 2x1.2 mA.

**Status outputs (slow / test):** `err_cnt<9:0>` (number of errored 4-bit words after lock), `err_ovf` (sticky counter overflow), `bist_lock` (15 consecutive clean words), `bist_err` (registered per-word error flag), `bist_busy`, `bist_done`.

**Blocks**

| block (cell) | function | HS path? |
|---|---|---|
| `bist_bias` | ibias diode, RC filter, power-down → vbn | no (bias) |
| `bist_clkgen` (`ck_rx_acbuf`, `inv_x4`, `dffr_x1` div2, `rxck_dly`/`dly_cell`) | AC-coupled self-biased clock RX, buffers, /2 word clock, RX clock delay trim | clock path |
| `mode_reg` | 9b parallel-load config register | no |
| `bist_ctrl` | start/stop/err_inj synchronizers, RUN/DONE flops, gen_run/chk_run/inj_p/clr_b | no |
| `prbs_gen` (`icg_x1`, 15 state flops, `prbs_pred4`) | 4-bit-per-word parallel PRBS7/15 LFSR, clock gated by gen_run, bit-0 error-inject XOR | no (digital word-rate source) |
| `bist_tx_hs` → `ser4to1` (dff retime, dlat alignment latches, `mux2_x1` 4:2 at wclk, ck latches, `ser_mux2_cml` 2:1 at ck) → `tx_cml_drv` | 4:1 serializer and CML line driver; bit order d<0> first | **yes** |
| `lpbk_mux` | RX termination, loopback tap, CML 2:1 select (lpbk_en) | **yes** |
| `bist_rx_hs` → `rx_ctle` → 2x `rx_sampler` (`sa_strongarm` + `sr_latch_nand`) → `rx_deser` | CTLE, even (rck) / odd (rckb) StrongARM samplers, 2→4 deserializer, rwclk generation | **yes** (deser output is word-rate) |
| `prbs_chk` (15-bit history, `prbs_pred4`, 4 XOR compare, OR4, err flop, sync2 of chk_run) | self-synchronizing checker → bist_err | no |
| `lock_det4` | 4b saturating clean-word counter → bist_lock | no |
| `err_cnt10` | 10b ripple counter of error words (gated by lock & run & !ovf) + sticky overflow | no |

---

## 2. zqcal.sp: ZQ calibration

**Top cell:** `zqcal_top`

**Supplies:** `vdd` = 0.8 V core logic and comparator latch; `vddq` = 1.1 V IO (replica legs, level shifters, VREF ladder, preamp; thick-oxide nch_18/pch_18); `vss`.

**There are no high-speed data inputs or outputs.** This is a slow mixed-signal calibration loop. Analog nodes:
- `zq`: the ZQ pad. An external RZQ = 240 Ohm to VSS sits off-chip. The pull-up replica array drives the pad, and the comparator senses it through a 1 kOhm isolation resistor (zq_s).
- Internal `npd`: the pull-down calibration node, made of the replica PU array (calibrated PU code) over the PD replica array.
- Internal `vref`: VDDQ/2 (trim selectable).

**Clock:** `zq_clk` (about 200 MHz) is the FSM/prescaler clock. Derived clocks: step_clk = zq_clk/8 (sequencer and SAR registers); cmp_clk = the 8th zq_clk period of each step, while busy (comparator strobe).

**Control inputs**
- `zq_start`: calibration start command (synchronized, edge-detected, ignored while busy).
- `zq_latch`: transfers the SAR results to the DQ driver code registers. It takes effect only when `zq_done`=1.
- `rstb`: async reset. The output codes reset to mid-scale 100000 (bit 5 uses a set flop).
- `vref_trim<1:0>`: VREF ladder tap. 00 = 15/32, 01 = 16/32 (nominal VDDQ/2), 10 = 17/32, 11 = 18/32 of VDDQ.

**Bias:** `ibias_zq` is a 10 uA reference current into the diode in `zq_bias`. It produces the tail bias for the comparator preamp.

**Code outputs (to the DQ drivers):** `pu_code<5:0>` and `pd_code<5:0>` are binary codes; 1 enables a leg. The leg weights are 32/16/8/4/2/1 units on top of an always-on 32-unit base leg. One unit is about 15.4 kOhm, so code 32 gives about 240 Ohm.

**Status:** `zq_busy`, `zq_done`, and `zq_cmp_mon` (comparator decision, test monitor; it also feeds both SARs).

**Algorithm:** the sequence is w0, w1 (analog settle), tu<5..0> (PU SAR), td<5..0> (PD SAR), done. The PU SAR sets trial bit k when the token is on bit k+1. When the token is on bit k, it keeps the bit if cmp=1. The PU phase compares vref against zq (cmp=1 means V(zq) < vref, so the PU is still too weak). The PD phase swaps the comparator inputs through `zq_inmux` and compares npd against vref (cmp=1 means V(npd) > vref, so the PD is still too weak). The decision polarity is therefore the same in both phases. en_pu powers the pad PU array during w0..tu0. en_pd powers the replica PU+PD branch during td5..td0.

**Blocks**

| block | function |
|---|---|
| `zq_fsm` | /8 ripple prescaler, start sync+edge, busy/done, 15-stage one-hot sequencer, en_pu/en_pd decode, cmp_clk |
| `zq_sar6` ×2 (`zq_sar_bit` = mux2 + or2 + dffr) | 6b SAR registers pu_b<5:0> and pd_b<5:0> |
| `zq_code_reg` | DQ driver code registers (pu_code, pd_code), loaded by zq_latch & zq_done |
| `zq_pu_cal_path` (`zq_predrv` → `zq_pu_array` → `zq_pu_unit`, `zq_pad_esd`) | pad pull-up replica, code-gated level-shifted gates, ESD, sense tap |
| `zq_pd_cal_path` (2x `zq_predrv`, `zq_pu_array`, `zq_pd_array`) | pull-down calibration divider, node npd |
| `zq_vref_gen` (`zq_ls`, `zq_vref_ladder`, `zq_vref_mux`, RC filter) | VDDQ/2 reference with 2b trim, power-gated |
| `zq_cmp_top` (`zq_bias`, `zq_inmux`, `zq_cmp` = `zq_preamp` + `zq_sa_latch` + `sr_latch_nand`) | phase-swapped comparator |

No block is on a high-speed data path. The analog decision path is zq/npd/vref → inmux → preamp → latch → cmp_q → SAR.

---

## 3. dqs_rx.sp: DQS/DQ byte receive path

**Top cell:** `dqs_dq_rx_top`

**Supplies:** `vddq` = 1.1 V (pads/ESD, DQS amp, DQ preamps, VREFDQ ladder/buffer, bias mirror; thick-oxide nch_18/pch_18); `vdd` = 0.8 V core (DQS C2C, WDCA, repeater tree, local clock buffers, VGAs, samplers, decoders); `vss`.

**High-speed data in:** `dq<7:0>`. These are single-ended POD-style DQ inputs, each compared with VREFDQ.
**High-speed data out:** `dq_r<7:0>` (data sampled on the DQS_t rising edge, the even bits) and `dq_f<7:0>` (data sampled on the DQS_c rising edge, i.e. the DQS_t falling edge, the odd bits). Each one is held by an SR latch for a full strobe cycle.
**Strobe in:** `dqs_t` / `dqs_c` (differential DQS/DQSB).

**Control codes and enables**
- `wdca<3:0>`: write duty-cycle adjust, built into the DQS buffer. `wdca<3>` is the sign: 1 widens the DQS_t high phase and 0 narrows it. `wdca<2:0>` is the magnitude, a binary-weighted 1/2/4 skew-leg strength. On the t rail, sign=1 enables extra pull-up legs; on the c rail it enables extra pull-down legs. Sign=0 does the reverse. `wdca_en`=0 forces no adjustment.
- `vga_gain<2:0>`: shared by all 8 bits. Each bit switches a degeneration resistor in parallel (bit0: 4k, bit1: 2k, bit2: 1k, over a 4k base). More resistance switched in lowers Rdeg and raises the gain (about 0.6x to 1.6x).
- `vref_code<3:0>`: VREFDQ = (40+code)/64 × VDDQ, i.e. 0.625 to 0.859 VDDQ in 1.56 % steps.
- `vref_en`: VREFDQ ladder header (via level shifter) and buffer enable.
- `rx_en`: bias generator, DQ preamp/VGA tails, and the per-bit local DQS clock gating. When it is 0, all sampler clocks are held low (precharge).
- `dqs_en`: DQS amp and C2C tail enable.

**Bias:** `ibias` is a 50 uA reference current into `rx_bias`. It produces vbn_c (nch_lvt tails: VGA, C2C) and vbn_q (nch_18 tails: DQ preamp, DQS amp, VREF buffer).

**Strobe path (unmatched):** dqs_t/dqs_c → `rx_esd` → `dqs_amp` → `dqs_c2c` (inverting) → `wdca_stage` (inverting, duty skew) → dqs_t_i/dqs_c_i → `dqs_clk_tree`. The tree has a trunk `rpt_stage`. The left branch (2 RPT plus RC wire) feeds the spine for DQ3, DQ2, DQ1, DQ0. The right branch (2 RPT plus RC wire) feeds the spine for DQ4, DQ5, DQ6, DQ7. Each bit has its own `dqs_lcb` (non-inverting, gated by rx_en), which drives dqs_t_b<k>/dqs_c_b<k>. No delay matching to DQ is applied; the RC spine gives each bit a different strobe arrival time.

**Data path, per bit (`dq_rx_bit`):** dq → `rx_esd` → `dq_preamp` (vs RC-filtered vref_buf) → `dq_vga` → two `dq_sampler` (`dq_sa` StrongARM + `sr_latch_nand` + driver). One is clocked by dqs_t_b and produces dq_r; the other is clocked by dqs_c_b and produces dq_f.

**Blocks not on the high-speed path:** `rx_bias`; `vrefdq_gen` (`ls_vdd2vddq`, `vref_ladder16`, `vref_dec4to16`/`pdec2to4`, `vref_sw16`, `vref_ota_buf`); `wdca_dec` (static code decoder, though it controls a block that is on the strobe path); the enable gating inside `dqs_lcb` (static).
`````

** Library name: hsio_bist_lib
** Cell name: prbs_gen
** View name: schematic

xi2<7> tx_d<1> gclk rstb r<7> net071<7> vdd vss dffr_x1
xi2<8> r<4> gclk rstb r<8> net071<8> vdd vss dffr_x1
xi2<9> r<5> gclk rstb r<9> net071<9> vdd vss dffr_x1
xi2<10> r<6> gclk rstb r<10> net071<10> vdd vss dffr_x1
xi2<11> r<7> gclk rstb r<11> net071<11> vdd vss dffr_x1
xi2<12> r<8> gclk rstb r<12> net071<12> vdd vss dffr_x1
xi2<13> r<9> gclk rstb r<13> net071<13> vdd vss dffr_x1
xi2<14> r<10> gclk rstb r<14> net071<14> vdd vss dffr_x1
xi2<15> r<11> gclk rstb r<15> net071<15> vdd vss dffr_x1
xi3 r<15> r<14> r<13> r<12> r<11> r<7> r<6> r<5> r<4> tx_d<1> prbs_sel p<3> p<2> p<1> p<0> vdd vss prbs_pred4
xi4 r<4> inj tx_d<0> vdd vss xor2_x1
.ends prbs_gen

xi1<15> c<11> rwclk c<15> net080<15> vdd vss dff_x1

### FILE: tests/regression/t2_dqs_rx/answer_key_README.md
<!-- sha256=28d00da03242c175398dfdcb87509629faa82a82f4bdcb62ff545fcea4148cc9 newline=1 -->
`````markdown
# Answer keys

There is one JSON file per netlist: `bist.json` (`../bist.sp`), `zqcal.json` (`../zqcal.sp`) and `dqs_rx.json` (`../dqs_rx.sp`). Each one is the ground truth for checking a block diagram drawn from that netlist.

**Top-level fields**
- `top`: the top cell.
- `supplies` / `grounds`: supply and ground net names.
- `ports`: one entry per top-level port. A bus is grouped as `name<msb:lsb>`. Each entry has a `class` (`hs_data_in`, `hs_data_out`, `clock_in`, `clock_out`, `important_control`, `general_control`, `bias`, `power`, `slow_signal` or `test_digital`) and a one-line `function`.

**`cells`**

The keys cover every cell that contains subcircuit instances, plus the leaf cells on the high-speed, clock or strobe path (and a few other notable leaf cells). Each cell has these fields:
- `role`: what the block is.
- `on_high_speed_path`: whether the block carries the high-speed data, clock or strobe.
- `inverting`: the polarity from main input to main output. `null` means it does not apply (logic or control blocks).
- `children`: the subcircuit instances only. Iterated instances are grouped, e.g. `xi0<3:0>`. Direct MOS, R and C devices are not listed as children. Their counts are appended at the end of `notes` as `[direct primitives in this cell: ...]`.
- `signal_flow`: rows of `[from, to, net, class]` in rough flow order.
  - `from` and `to` are written as `<inst>.<pin>`. `PORT.<pin>` means the cell's own port. In leaf cells, a device terminal is written as `mn0.g` (MOS d/g/s/b) or `r0.p` / `r0.n` (first / second node of an R or C).
  - `net` is the net name inside that cell.
  - `class` is one of `hs_data`, `word_data`, `clock`, `strobe`, `analog`, `reference`, `bias`, `control`, `code`, `decision`, `status`, `data` or `logic`.
  - For buses and repeated bit slices, only representative bits are listed (for example `<0>` and `<3>`). The other bits are wired the same way.
- `controls`: each control net or bus, and what it sets.
- `notes`: feedback loops, unused outputs, deliberate asymmetry and other things a reviewer needs to know.

Every `from`/`to` pair in `signal_flow` was checked by script against the netlist. Both ends resolve to the stated net.
`````

### FILE: tests/regression/t2_dqs_rx/intent.md
<!-- sha256=f10d339ce64990a4469ac36d7f167552ef1c739d4a201f49f1e86e4654eab048 newline=1 -->
`````markdown
# Designer intent notes

All three netlists are HSPICE (hspiceD-style) schematic exports. The top cell of each one is a `.subckt` that nothing else instantiates. Device models (`nch`, `pch`, `nch_lvt`, `pch_lvt`, `nch_18`, `pch_18`) come from the PDK and are not included. Every subcircuit is defined in its own file. Bus pins are written MSB first.

---

## 1. bist.sp: HSIO loopback BIST

**Top cell:** `hsio_bist_top`

**Supplies:** `vdd` = 0.9 V core (logic, clocks, samplers); `vddq` = 1.0 V (CML serializer output, TX driver, loopback mux, CTLE); `vss`.

**High-speed data**
- Out: `txp` / `txn`. These are the CML TX pads (50 Ohm back-terminated to vddq). The PRBS pattern leaves the chip here.
- In: `rxp` / `rxn`. These are the external RX pads (2x50 Ohm termination to a self-biased CM node of 0.7*vddq). The loopback mux selects them when `lpbk_en`=0.
- Internal loopback: the TX pads `txp/txn` are tapped through 200 Ohm series resistors into the second input of the loopback mux.

**Clock inputs:** `ckp` / `ckn` is the 4 GHz half-rate differential clock (8 Gb/s, DDR). From it the chip derives: ck/ckb (serializer final mux), wclk/wclkb = ck/2 (TX word clock, 4 bits/word), rck/rckb (RX sampling clock = ck through the delay trim), and rwclk/rwclkb = rck/2 (RX word clock).

**Control**
- `cfg<8:0>` + `cfg_wr` (rising edge writes) feed the mode register:
  - `cfg<8>` prbs_sel: 0 = PRBS7 (x^7+x^6+1), 1 = PRBS15 (x^15+x^14+1), for both the generator and the checker.
  - `cfg<7>` lpbk_en: 1 = internal TX→RX loopback, 0 = external rxp/rxn.
  - `cfg<6>` tx_en: enables the TX CML driver tail, and the generator runs only when it is set.
  - `cfg<5>` rx_en: CTLE tail enable.
  - `cfg<4>` chk_en: checker run enable.
  - `cfg<3>` err_inj: a 0→1 write injects a single bit error, by inverting tx_d<0> for one word.
  - `cfg<2:0>` rdly<2:0>: binary-weighted switched-cap delay trim of the RX sampling clock (rck/rckb) relative to the TX clock. This sets the sampling phase in loopback.
- `bist_start`, `bist_stop`: asynchronous level/edge requests, synchronized to wclk. Start sets RUN and clears the error counter and lock detector (clr_b pulse). Stop clears RUN and sets DONE.
- `rstb`: global active-low asynchronous reset. It also seeds the LFSR with 0...01.
- `bist_en`: bias enable.

**Bias:** `ibias` is a 100 uA reference current into the diode in `bist_bias`. It produces `vbn` for all CML tails: ser mux 1.6 mA, TX driver 8 mA, loopback mux 1.6 mA, CTLE 2x1.2 mA.

**Status outputs (slow / test):** `err_cnt<9:0>` (number of errored 4-bit words after lock), `err_ovf` (sticky counter overflow), `bist_lock` (15 consecutive clean words), `bist_err` (registered per-word error flag), `bist_busy`, `bist_done`.

**Blocks**

| block (cell) | function | HS path? |
|---|---|---|
| `bist_bias` | ibias diode, RC filter, power-down → vbn | no (bias) |
| `bist_clkgen` (`ck_rx_acbuf`, `inv_x4`, `dffr_x1` div2, `rxck_dly`/`dly_cell`) | AC-coupled self-biased clock RX, buffers, /2 word clock, RX clock delay trim | clock path |
| `mode_reg` | 9b parallel-load config register | no |
| `bist_ctrl` | start/stop/err_inj synchronizers, RUN/DONE flops, gen_run/chk_run/inj_p/clr_b | no |
| `prbs_gen` (`icg_x1`, 15 state flops, `prbs_pred4`) | 4-bit-per-word parallel PRBS7/15 LFSR, clock gated by gen_run, bit-0 error-inject XOR | no (digital word-rate source) |
| `bist_tx_hs` → `ser4to1` (dff retime, dlat alignment latches, `mux2_x1` 4:2 at wclk, ck latches, `ser_mux2_cml` 2:1 at ck) → `tx_cml_drv` | 4:1 serializer and CML line driver; bit order d<0> first | **yes** |
| `lpbk_mux` | RX termination, loopback tap, CML 2:1 select (lpbk_en) | **yes** |
| `bist_rx_hs` → `rx_ctle` → 2x `rx_sampler` (`sa_strongarm` + `sr_latch_nand`) → `rx_deser` | CTLE, even (rck) / odd (rckb) StrongARM samplers, 2→4 deserializer, rwclk generation | **yes** (deser output is word-rate) |
| `prbs_chk` (15-bit history, `prbs_pred4`, 4 XOR compare, OR4, err flop, sync2 of chk_run) | self-synchronizing checker → bist_err | no |
| `lock_det4` | 4b saturating clean-word counter → bist_lock | no |
| `err_cnt10` | 10b ripple counter of error words (gated by lock & run & !ovf) + sticky overflow | no |

---

## 2. zqcal.sp: ZQ calibration

**Top cell:** `zqcal_top`

**Supplies:** `vdd` = 0.8 V core logic and comparator latch; `vddq` = 1.1 V IO (replica legs, level shifters, VREF ladder, preamp; thick-oxide nch_18/pch_18); `vss`.

**There are no high-speed data inputs or outputs.** This is a slow mixed-signal calibration loop. Analog nodes:
- `zq`: the ZQ pad. An external RZQ = 240 Ohm to VSS sits off-chip. The pull-up replica array drives the pad, and the comparator senses it through a 1 kOhm isolation resistor (zq_s).
- Internal `npd`: the pull-down calibration node, made of the replica PU array (calibrated PU code) over the PD replica array.
- Internal `vref`: VDDQ/2 (trim selectable).

**Clock:** `zq_clk` (about 200 MHz) is the FSM/prescaler clock. Derived clocks: step_clk = zq_clk/8 (sequencer and SAR registers); cmp_clk = the 8th zq_clk period of each step, while busy (comparator strobe).

**Control inputs**
- `zq_start`: calibration start command (synchronized, edge-detected, ignored while busy).
- `zq_latch`: transfers the SAR results to the DQ driver code registers. It takes effect only when `zq_done`=1.
- `rstb`: async reset. The output codes reset to mid-scale 100000 (bit 5 uses a set flop).
- `vref_trim<1:0>`: VREF ladder tap. 00 = 15/32, 01 = 16/32 (nominal VDDQ/2), 10 = 17/32, 11 = 18/32 of VDDQ.

**Bias:** `ibias_zq` is a 10 uA reference current into the diode in `zq_bias`. It produces the tail bias for the comparator preamp.

**Code outputs (to the DQ drivers):** `pu_code<5:0>` and `pd_code<5:0>` are binary codes; 1 enables a leg. The leg weights are 32/16/8/4/2/1 units on top of an always-on 32-unit base leg. One unit is about 15.4 kOhm, so code 32 gives about 240 Ohm.

**Status:** `zq_busy`, `zq_done`, and `zq_cmp_mon` (comparator decision, test monitor; it also feeds both SARs).

**Algorithm:** the sequence is w0, w1 (analog settle), tu<5..0> (PU SAR), td<5..0> (PD SAR), done. The PU SAR sets trial bit k when the token is on bit k+1. When the token is on bit k, it keeps the bit if cmp=1. The PU phase compares vref against zq (cmp=1 means V(zq) < vref, so the PU is still too weak). The PD phase swaps the comparator inputs through `zq_inmux` and compares npd against vref (cmp=1 means V(npd) > vref, so the PD is still too weak). The decision polarity is therefore the same in both phases. en_pu powers the pad PU array during w0..tu0. en_pd powers the replica PU+PD branch during td5..td0.

**Blocks**

| block | function |
|---|---|
| `zq_fsm` | /8 ripple prescaler, start sync+edge, busy/done, 15-stage one-hot sequencer, en_pu/en_pd decode, cmp_clk |
| `zq_sar6` ×2 (`zq_sar_bit` = mux2 + or2 + dffr) | 6b SAR registers pu_b<5:0> and pd_b<5:0> |
| `zq_code_reg` | DQ driver code registers (pu_code, pd_code), loaded by zq_latch & zq_done |
| `zq_pu_cal_path` (`zq_predrv` → `zq_pu_array` → `zq_pu_unit`, `zq_pad_esd`) | pad pull-up replica, code-gated level-shifted gates, ESD, sense tap |
| `zq_pd_cal_path` (2x `zq_predrv`, `zq_pu_array`, `zq_pd_array`) | pull-down calibration divider, node npd |
| `zq_vref_gen` (`zq_ls`, `zq_vref_ladder`, `zq_vref_mux`, RC filter) | VDDQ/2 reference with 2b trim, power-gated |
| `zq_cmp_top` (`zq_bias`, `zq_inmux`, `zq_cmp` = `zq_preamp` + `zq_sa_latch` + `sr_latch_nand`) | phase-swapped comparator |

No block is on a high-speed data path. The analog decision path is zq/npd/vref → inmux → preamp → latch → cmp_q → SAR.

---

## 3. dqs_rx.sp: DQS/DQ byte receive path

**Top cell:** `dqs_dq_rx_top`

**Supplies:** `vddq` = 1.1 V (pads/ESD, DQS amp, DQ preamps, VREFDQ ladder/buffer, bias mirror; thick-oxide nch_18/pch_18); `vdd` = 0.8 V core (DQS C2C, WDCA, repeater tree, local clock buffers, VGAs, samplers, decoders); `vss`.

**High-speed data in:** `dq<7:0>`. These are single-ended POD-style DQ inputs, each compared with VREFDQ.
**High-speed data out:** `dq_r<7:0>` (data sampled on the DQS_t rising edge, the even bits) and `dq_f<7:0>` (data sampled on the DQS_c rising edge, i.e. the DQS_t falling edge, the odd bits). Each one is held by an SR latch for a full strobe cycle.
**Strobe in:** `dqs_t` / `dqs_c` (differential DQS/DQSB).

**Control codes and enables**
- `wdca<3:0>`: write duty-cycle adjust, built into the DQS buffer. `wdca<3>` is the sign: 1 widens the DQS_t high phase and 0 narrows it. `wdca<2:0>` is the magnitude, a binary-weighted 1/2/4 skew-leg strength. On the t rail, sign=1 enables extra pull-up legs; on the c rail it enables extra pull-down legs. Sign=0 does the reverse. `wdca_en`=0 forces no adjustment.
- `vga_gain<2:0>`: shared by all 8 bits. Each bit switches a degeneration resistor in parallel (bit0: 4k, bit1: 2k, bit2: 1k, over a 4k base). More resistance switched in lowers Rdeg and raises the gain (about 0.6x to 1.6x).
- `vref_code<3:0>`: VREFDQ = (40+code)/64 × VDDQ, i.e. 0.625 to 0.859 VDDQ in 1.56 % steps.
- `vref_en`: VREFDQ ladder header (via level shifter) and buffer enable.
- `rx_en`: bias generator, DQ preamp/VGA tails, and the per-bit local DQS clock gating. When it is 0, all sampler clocks are held low (precharge).
- `dqs_en`: DQS amp and C2C tail enable.

**Bias:** `ibias` is a 50 uA reference current into `rx_bias`. It produces vbn_c (nch_lvt tails: VGA, C2C) and vbn_q (nch_18 tails: DQ preamp, DQS amp, VREF buffer).

**Strobe path (unmatched):** dqs_t/dqs_c → `rx_esd` → `dqs_amp` → `dqs_c2c` (inverting) → `wdca_stage` (inverting, duty skew) → dqs_t_i/dqs_c_i → `dqs_clk_tree`. The tree has a trunk `rpt_stage`. The left branch (2 RPT plus RC wire) feeds the spine for DQ3, DQ2, DQ1, DQ0. The right branch (2 RPT plus RC wire) feeds the spine for DQ4, DQ5, DQ6, DQ7. Each bit has its own `dqs_lcb` (non-inverting, gated by rx_en), which drives dqs_t_b<k>/dqs_c_b<k>. No delay matching to DQ is applied; the RC spine gives each bit a different strobe arrival time.

**Data path, per bit (`dq_rx_bit`):** dq → `rx_esd` → `dq_preamp` (vs RC-filtered vref_buf) → `dq_vga` → two `dq_sampler` (`dq_sa` StrongARM + `sr_latch_nand` + driver). One is clocked by dqs_t_b and produces dq_r; the other is clocked by dqs_c_b and produces dq_f.

**Blocks not on the high-speed path:** `rx_bias`; `vrefdq_gen` (`ls_vdd2vddq`, `vref_ladder16`, `vref_dec4to16`/`pdec2to4`, `vref_sw16`, `vref_ota_buf`); `wdca_dec` (static code decoder, though it controls a block that is on the strobe path); the enable gating inside `dqs_lcb` (static).
`````

    ["PORT.a", "xi0.a", "a", "logic"],
    ["xi0.y", "xi1.a", "net6", "logic"],
    ["xi1.y", "PORT.y", "y", "logic"]
   ],
   "controls": {},
   "notes": ""
  }
 }
}

### FILE: tests/regression/t2_zqcal/answer_key_README.md
<!-- sha256=28d00da03242c175398dfdcb87509629faa82a82f4bdcb62ff545fcea4148cc9 newline=1 -->
`````markdown
# Answer keys

There is one JSON file per netlist: `bist.json` (`../bist.sp`), `zqcal.json` (`../zqcal.sp`) and `dqs_rx.json` (`../dqs_rx.sp`). Each one is the ground truth for checking a block diagram drawn from that netlist.

**Top-level fields**
- `top`: the top cell.
- `supplies` / `grounds`: supply and ground net names.
- `ports`: one entry per top-level port. A bus is grouped as `name<msb:lsb>`. Each entry has a `class` (`hs_data_in`, `hs_data_out`, `clock_in`, `clock_out`, `important_control`, `general_control`, `bias`, `power`, `slow_signal` or `test_digital`) and a one-line `function`.

**`cells`**

The keys cover every cell that contains subcircuit instances, plus the leaf cells on the high-speed, clock or strobe path (and a few other notable leaf cells). Each cell has these fields:
- `role`: what the block is.
- `on_high_speed_path`: whether the block carries the high-speed data, clock or strobe.
- `inverting`: the polarity from main input to main output. `null` means it does not apply (logic or control blocks).
- `children`: the subcircuit instances only. Iterated instances are grouped, e.g. `xi0<3:0>`. Direct MOS, R and C devices are not listed as children. Their counts are appended at the end of `notes` as `[direct primitives in this cell: ...]`.
- `signal_flow`: rows of `[from, to, net, class]` in rough flow order.
  - `from` and `to` are written as `<inst>.<pin>`. `PORT.<pin>` means the cell's own port. In leaf cells, a device terminal is written as `mn0.g` (MOS d/g/s/b) or `r0.p` / `r0.n` (first / second node of an R or C).
  - `net` is the net name inside that cell.
  - `class` is one of `hs_data`, `word_data`, `clock`, `strobe`, `analog`, `reference`, `bias`, `control`, `code`, `decision`, `status`, `data` or `logic`.
  - For buses and repeated bit slices, only representative bits are listed (for example `<0>` and `<3>`). The other bits are wired the same way.
- `controls`: each control net or bus, and what it sets.
- `notes`: feedback loops, unused outputs, deliberate asymmetry and other things a reviewer needs to know.

Every `from`/`to` pair in `signal_flow` was checked by script against the netlist. Both ends resolve to the stated net.
`````

### FILE: tests/regression/t2_zqcal/intent.md
<!-- sha256=f10d339ce64990a4469ac36d7f167552ef1c739d4a201f49f1e86e4654eab048 newline=1 -->
`````markdown
# Designer intent notes

All three netlists are HSPICE (hspiceD-style) schematic exports. The top cell of each one is a `.subckt` that nothing else instantiates. Device models (`nch`, `pch`, `nch_lvt`, `pch_lvt`, `nch_18`, `pch_18`) come from the PDK and are not included. Every subcircuit is defined in its own file. Bus pins are written MSB first.

---

## 1. bist.sp: HSIO loopback BIST

**Top cell:** `hsio_bist_top`

**Supplies:** `vdd` = 0.9 V core (logic, clocks, samplers); `vddq` = 1.0 V (CML serializer output, TX driver, loopback mux, CTLE); `vss`.

**High-speed data**
- Out: `txp` / `txn`. These are the CML TX pads (50 Ohm back-terminated to vddq). The PRBS pattern leaves the chip here.
- In: `rxp` / `rxn`. These are the external RX pads (2x50 Ohm termination to a self-biased CM node of 0.7*vddq). The loopback mux selects them when `lpbk_en`=0.
- Internal loopback: the TX pads `txp/txn` are tapped through 200 Ohm series resistors into the second input of the loopback mux.

**Clock inputs:** `ckp` / `ckn` is the 4 GHz half-rate differential clock (8 Gb/s, DDR). From it the chip derives: ck/ckb (serializer final mux), wclk/wclkb = ck/2 (TX word clock, 4 bits/word), rck/rckb (RX sampling clock = ck through the delay trim), and rwclk/rwclkb = rck/2 (RX word clock).

**Control**
- `cfg<8:0>` + `cfg_wr` (rising edge writes) feed the mode register:
  - `cfg<8>` prbs_sel: 0 = PRBS7 (x^7+x^6+1), 1 = PRBS15 (x^15+x^14+1), for both the generator and the checker.
  - `cfg<7>` lpbk_en: 1 = internal TX→RX loopback, 0 = external rxp/rxn.
  - `cfg<6>` tx_en: enables the TX CML driver tail, and the generator runs only when it is set.
  - `cfg<5>` rx_en: CTLE tail enable.
  - `cfg<4>` chk_en: checker run enable.
  - `cfg<3>` err_inj: a 0→1 write injects a single bit error, by inverting tx_d<0> for one word.
  - `cfg<2:0>` rdly<2:0>: binary-weighted switched-cap delay trim of the RX sampling clock (rck/rckb) relative to the TX clock. This sets the sampling phase in loopback.
- `bist_start`, `bist_stop`: asynchronous level/edge requests, synchronized to wclk. Start sets RUN and clears the error counter and lock detector (clr_b pulse). Stop clears RUN and sets DONE.
- `rstb`: global active-low asynchronous reset. It also seeds the LFSR with 0...01.
- `bist_en`: bias enable.

**Bias:** `ibias` is a 100 uA reference current into the diode in `bist_bias`. It produces `vbn` for all CML tails: ser mux 1.6 mA, TX driver 8 mA, loopback mux 1.6 mA, CTLE 2x1.2 mA.

**Status outputs (slow / test):** `err_cnt<9:0>` (number of errored 4-bit words after lock), `err_ovf` (sticky counter overflow), `bist_lock` (15 consecutive clean words), `bist_err` (registered per-word error flag), `bist_busy`, `bist_done`.

**Blocks**

| block (cell) | function | HS path? |
|---|---|---|
| `bist_bias` | ibias diode, RC filter, power-down → vbn | no (bias) |
| `bist_clkgen` (`ck_rx_acbuf`, `inv_x4`, `dffr_x1` div2, `rxck_dly`/`dly_cell`) | AC-coupled self-biased clock RX, buffers, /2 word clock, RX clock delay trim | clock path |
| `mode_reg` | 9b parallel-load config register | no |
| `bist_ctrl` | start/stop/err_inj synchronizers, RUN/DONE flops, gen_run/chk_run/inj_p/clr_b | no |
| `prbs_gen` (`icg_x1`, 15 state flops, `prbs_pred4`) | 4-bit-per-word parallel PRBS7/15 LFSR, clock gated by gen_run, bit-0 error-inject XOR | no (digital word-rate source) |
| `bist_tx_hs` → `ser4to1` (dff retime, dlat alignment latches, `mux2_x1` 4:2 at wclk, ck latches, `ser_mux2_cml` 2:1 at ck) → `tx_cml_drv` | 4:1 serializer and CML line driver; bit order d<0> first | **yes** |
| `lpbk_mux` | RX termination, loopback tap, CML 2:1 select (lpbk_en) | **yes** |
| `bist_rx_hs` → `rx_ctle` → 2x `rx_sampler` (`sa_strongarm` + `sr_latch_nand`) → `rx_deser` | CTLE, even (rck) / odd (rckb) StrongARM samplers, 2→4 deserializer, rwclk generation | **yes** (deser output is word-rate) |
| `prbs_chk` (15-bit history, `prbs_pred4`, 4 XOR compare, OR4, err flop, sync2 of chk_run) | self-synchronizing checker → bist_err | no |
| `lock_det4` | 4b saturating clean-word counter → bist_lock | no |
| `err_cnt10` | 10b ripple counter of error words (gated by lock & run & !ovf) + sticky overflow | no |

---

## 2. zqcal.sp: ZQ calibration

**Top cell:** `zqcal_top`

**Supplies:** `vdd` = 0.8 V core logic and comparator latch; `vddq` = 1.1 V IO (replica legs, level shifters, VREF ladder, preamp; thick-oxide nch_18/pch_18); `vss`.

**There are no high-speed data inputs or outputs.** This is a slow mixed-signal calibration loop. Analog nodes:
- `zq`: the ZQ pad. An external RZQ = 240 Ohm to VSS sits off-chip. The pull-up replica array drives the pad, and the comparator senses it through a 1 kOhm isolation resistor (zq_s).
- Internal `npd`: the pull-down calibration node, made of the replica PU array (calibrated PU code) over the PD replica array.
- Internal `vref`: VDDQ/2 (trim selectable).

**Clock:** `zq_clk` (about 200 MHz) is the FSM/prescaler clock. Derived clocks: step_clk = zq_clk/8 (sequencer and SAR registers); cmp_clk = the 8th zq_clk period of each step, while busy (comparator strobe).

**Control inputs**
- `zq_start`: calibration start command (synchronized, edge-detected, ignored while busy).
- `zq_latch`: transfers the SAR results to the DQ driver code registers. It takes effect only when `zq_done`=1.
- `rstb`: async reset. The output codes reset to mid-scale 100000 (bit 5 uses a set flop).
- `vref_trim<1:0>`: VREF ladder tap. 00 = 15/32, 01 = 16/32 (nominal VDDQ/2), 10 = 17/32, 11 = 18/32 of VDDQ.

**Bias:** `ibias_zq` is a 10 uA reference current into the diode in `zq_bias`. It produces the tail bias for the comparator preamp.

**Code outputs (to the DQ drivers):** `pu_code<5:0>` and `pd_code<5:0>` are binary codes; 1 enables a leg. The leg weights are 32/16/8/4/2/1 units on top of an always-on 32-unit base leg. One unit is about 15.4 kOhm, so code 32 gives about 240 Ohm.

**Status:** `zq_busy`, `zq_done`, and `zq_cmp_mon` (comparator decision, test monitor; it also feeds both SARs).

**Algorithm:** the sequence is w0, w1 (analog settle), tu<5..0> (PU SAR), td<5..0> (PD SAR), done. The PU SAR sets trial bit k when the token is on bit k+1. When the token is on bit k, it keeps the bit if cmp=1. The PU phase compares vref against zq (cmp=1 means V(zq) < vref, so the PU is still too weak). The PD phase swaps the comparator inputs through `zq_inmux` and compares npd against vref (cmp=1 means V(npd) > vref, so the PD is still too weak). The decision polarity is therefore the same in both phases. en_pu powers the pad PU array during w0..tu0. en_pd powers the replica PU+PD branch during td5..td0.

**Blocks**

| block | function |
|---|---|
| `zq_fsm` | /8 ripple prescaler, start sync+edge, busy/done, 15-stage one-hot sequencer, en_pu/en_pd decode, cmp_clk |
| `zq_sar6` ×2 (`zq_sar_bit` = mux2 + or2 + dffr) | 6b SAR registers pu_b<5:0> and pd_b<5:0> |
| `zq_code_reg` | DQ driver code registers (pu_code, pd_code), loaded by zq_latch & zq_done |
| `zq_pu_cal_path` (`zq_predrv` → `zq_pu_array` → `zq_pu_unit`, `zq_pad_esd`) | pad pull-up replica, code-gated level-shifted gates, ESD, sense tap |
| `zq_pd_cal_path` (2x `zq_predrv`, `zq_pu_array`, `zq_pd_array`) | pull-down calibration divider, node npd |
| `zq_vref_gen` (`zq_ls`, `zq_vref_ladder`, `zq_vref_mux`, RC filter) | VDDQ/2 reference with 2b trim, power-gated |
| `zq_cmp_top` (`zq_bias`, `zq_inmux`, `zq_cmp` = `zq_preamp` + `zq_sa_latch` + `sr_latch_nand`) | phase-swapped comparator |

No block is on a high-speed data path. The analog decision path is zq/npd/vref → inmux → preamp → latch → cmp_q → SAR.

---

## 3. dqs_rx.sp: DQS/DQ byte receive path

**Top cell:** `dqs_dq_rx_top`

**Supplies:** `vddq` = 1.1 V (pads/ESD, DQS amp, DQ preamps, VREFDQ ladder/buffer, bias mirror; thick-oxide nch_18/pch_18); `vdd` = 0.8 V core (DQS C2C, WDCA, repeater tree, local clock buffers, VGAs, samplers, decoders); `vss`.

**High-speed data in:** `dq<7:0>`. These are single-ended POD-style DQ inputs, each compared with VREFDQ.
**High-speed data out:** `dq_r<7:0>` (data sampled on the DQS_t rising edge, the even bits) and `dq_f<7:0>` (data sampled on the DQS_c rising edge, i.e. the DQS_t falling edge, the odd bits). Each one is held by an SR latch for a full strobe cycle.
**Strobe in:** `dqs_t` / `dqs_c` (differential DQS/DQSB).

**Control codes and enables**
- `wdca<3:0>`: write duty-cycle adjust, built into the DQS buffer. `wdca<3>` is the sign: 1 widens the DQS_t high phase and 0 narrows it. `wdca<2:0>` is the magnitude, a binary-weighted 1/2/4 skew-leg strength. On the t rail, sign=1 enables extra pull-up legs; on the c rail it enables extra pull-down legs. Sign=0 does the reverse. `wdca_en`=0 forces no adjustment.
- `vga_gain<2:0>`: shared by all 8 bits. Each bit switches a degeneration resistor in parallel (bit0: 4k, bit1: 2k, bit2: 1k, over a 4k base). More resistance switched in lowers Rdeg and raises the gain (about 0.6x to 1.6x).
- `vref_code<3:0>`: VREFDQ = (40+code)/64 × VDDQ, i.e. 0.625 to 0.859 VDDQ in 1.56 % steps.
- `vref_en`: VREFDQ ladder header (via level shifter) and buffer enable.
- `rx_en`: bias generator, DQ preamp/VGA tails, and the per-bit local DQS clock gating. When it is 0, all sampler clocks are held low (precharge).
- `dqs_en`: DQS amp and C2C tail enable.

**Bias:** `ibias` is a 50 uA reference current into `rx_bias`. It produces vbn_c (nch_lvt tails: VGA, C2C) and vbn_q (nch_18 tails: DQ preamp, DQS amp, VREF buffer).

**Strobe path (unmatched):** dqs_t/dqs_c → `rx_esd` → `dqs_amp` → `dqs_c2c` (inverting) → `wdca_stage` (inverting, duty skew) → dqs_t_i/dqs_c_i → `dqs_clk_tree`. The tree has a trunk `rpt_stage`. The left branch (2 RPT plus RC wire) feeds the spine for DQ3, DQ2, DQ1, DQ0. The right branch (2 RPT plus RC wire) feeds the spine for DQ4, DQ5, DQ6, DQ7. Each bit has its own `dqs_lcb` (non-inverting, gated by rx_en), which drives dqs_t_b<k>/dqs_c_b<k>. No delay matching to DQ is applied; the RC spine gives each bit a different strobe arrival time.

**Data path, per bit (`dq_rx_bit`):** dq → `rx_esd` → `dq_preamp` (vs RC-filtered vref_buf) → `dq_vga` → two `dq_sampler` (`dq_sa` StrongARM + `sr_latch_nand` + driver). One is clocked by dqs_t_b and produces dq_r; the other is clocked by dqs_c_b and produces dq_f.

**Blocks not on the high-speed path:** `rx_bias`; `vrefdq_gen` (`ls_vdd2vddq`, `vref_ladder16`, `vref_dec4to16`/`pdec2to4`, `vref_sw16`, `vref_ota_buf`); `wdca_dec` (static code decoder, though it controls a block that is on the strobe path); the enable gating inside `dqs_lcb` (static).
`````

    "zq_en": "powers VREF divider, comparators (via enb_q) and enables replica gates",
    "zq_start": "starts PU successive approximation",
    "zq_rst_n": "resets SAR (code 0) and PD counter (10000)"
   },
   "notes": "Two feedback loops. PU: SAR code -> gate driver -> replica PMOS legs into the ZQ pin against external RZQ -> comparator (out=1 when ZQ > VREF, i.e. PU too strong) -> SAR clears the trial bit; 5 decisions after start, then zq_done. PD: counter code -> gate driver -> PD replica legs against an internal copy of the calibrated PU at npd -> comparator (out=1 when npd > VREF, PD too weak) -> count up; runs continuously once zq_done (dithers +/-1 LSB). pu_g<4:0> and pd_gb<4:0> gate-driver outputs are unused; the counter hold input is tied to vss. MM0 is the PMOS diode receiving ib_zq, giving the comparator tail bias. In nf_io_top zq_clk is the shared slow calibration clock cal_clk; pu_code/pd_code feed io_ctrl (drv_code_mux -> tx_ctrl -> leg enables of all DQ/DQS drivers) and are also read back as zq_pu_code/zq_pd_code. Replica unit is 1/8 of the driver unit, so the calibrated code gives Rpu = RZQ/8 at the pad (37.5 ohm for RZQ = 300 ohm)."
  },

  "rx_deser4": {
   "role": "1:4 deserializer per bit: retime the rise sample onto the fall strobe, capture (UI0,UI1) on div_p, re-register them and capture (UI2,UI3) on div_n so all four outputs update together",
   "on_high_speed_path": true,
   "inverting": false,
   "children": [
    {
     "inst": "XI0",
     "cell": "dff_tg",
     "role": "retime dr onto ckf -> e0"
    },
    {
     "inst": "XI1",
     "cell": "dff_tg",
     "role": "UI0 (e0) on div_p -> p0"
    },
    {
     "inst": "XI2",
     "cell": "dff_tg",
     "role": "UI1 (df) on div_p -> p1"
    },
    {
     "inst": "XI5",
     "cell": "dff_tg",
     "role": "rd<0> = p0 re-registered on div_n"
    },
    {
     "inst": "XI6",
     "cell": "dff_tg",
     "role": "rd<1> = p1 re-registered on div_n"
    },
    {
     "inst": "XI3",
     "cell": "dff_tg",
     "role": "rd<2> (UI2, e0) on div_n"
    },
    {
     "inst": "XI4",
     "cell": "dff_tg",
     "role": "rd<3> (UI3, df) on div_n"
    }
   ],
   "signal_flow": [
    [
     "PORT.dr",
     "XI0.d",
     "dr",
     "hs_data"
    ],
    [
     "PORT.ckf",
     "XI0.ck",
     "ckf",
     "clock"
    ],
    [
     "XI0.q",
     "XI1.d",
     "e0",
     "hs_data"
    ],
    [
     "XI0.q",
     "XI3.d",
     "e0",
     "hs_data"
    ],
    [
     "PORT.df",
     "XI2.d",
     "df",
     "hs_data"
    ],
    [
     "PORT.df",
     "XI4.d",
     "df",
     "hs_data"
    ],
    [
     "PORT.div_p",
     "XI1.ck",
     "div_p",
     "clock"
    ],
    [
     "PORT.div_p",
     "XI2.ck",
     "div_p",
     "clock"
    ],
    [
     "XI1.q",
     "XI5.d",
     "p0",
     "word_rate_data"
    ],
    [
     "XI2.q",
     "XI6.d",
     "p1",
     "word_rate_data"
    ],
    [
     "PORT.div_n",
     "XI5.ck",
     "div_n",
     "clock"
    ],
    [
     "PORT.div_n",
     "XI6.ck",
     "div_n",
     "clock"
    ],
    [
     "PORT.div_n",
     "XI3.ck",
     "div_n",
     "clock"
    ],
    [
     "PORT.div_n",
     "XI4.ck",
     "div_n",
     "clock"
    ],
    [
     "XI5.q",
     "PORT.rd<0>",
     "rd<0>",
     "word_rate_data"
    ],
    [
     "XI6.q",
     "PORT.rd<1>",
     "rd<1>",
     "word_rate_data"
    ],
    [
     "XI3.q",
     "PORT.rd<2>",
     "rd<2>",
     "word_rate_data"
    ],
    [
     "XI4.q",
     "PORT.rd<3>",
     "rd<3>",
     "word_rate_data"
    ]
   ],
   "controls": {},
   "notes": "(e0, df) is valid for one DQS period after each ckf edge. div_p rise captures UI0/UI1 into p0/p1; the next div_n rise (one DQS period later) captures UI2/UI3 and re-registers p0/p1, so rd<3:0> changes once per word (every 2 DQS periods) and the core can capture it on din_clk (= div_p) rising, mid-window. rd<0> is the first UI. Burst-to-word alignment depends on the divider reset phase (rx_rst_n release). Switch-level check: 11 random words reproduced in UI order."
  },

    {
     "inst": "XI1",
     "cell": "dffr_tg",
     "role": "previous decision up_d"
    },
    {
     "inst": "XI2",
     "cell": "dffr_tg",
     "role": "valid flag (d tied to vdd): ignores the first decision after reset"
    },
    {
     "inst": "XI3",
     "cell": "xor2_x1",
     "role": "decision change up ^ up_d"
    },
    {
     "inst": "XI4",
     "cell": "nand2_x1",
     "role": "dithb = ~(change & vld)"
    },
    {
     "inst": "XI5",
     "cell": "inv_x1",
     "role": "dith"
    },
    {
     "inst": "XI6",
     "cell": "nand2_x1",
     "role": "d0 = s0 | dith"
    },
    {
     "inst": "XI7",
     "cell": "dffr_tg",
     "role": "first dither seen (sticky)"
    },
    {
     "inst": "XI8",
     "cell": "nand2_x1",
     "role": "~(s0 & dith)"
    },
    {
     "inst": "XI9",
     "cell": "nand2_x1",
     "role": "d1 = lock | (s0 & dith)"
    },
    {
     "inst": "XI10",
     "cell": "dffr_tg",
     "role": "lock flag (sticky)"
    }
   ],

    "dcc_train": "1 = run DCC training (detector, update clock, counter enabled); 0 = code held, lock cleared",
    "dcc_rst_n": "resets the code to 10000 (neutral)",
    "dcc_code<4:0>": "DCA setting (loop state)"
   },
   "notes": "Closes the DCC loop through re_clk_path: dcc_code -> tx_dca -> RPT chain -> tree -> ck_dcc leaf -> dcc_det -> sa_cmp -> updn_cnt5 -> dcc_code. Duty > 50% -> vp > vn -> up=1 -> code counts up -> DCA PU legs shorten the high phase (negative feedback). Comparator evaluates on upd_clk rising, counter and lock detector update on upd_clk falling. After two valid dithers dcc_lock=1 drives hold. Comparator qb (net011) unused. Switch-level check with a behavioural duty model: locks within +/-1 LSB from both sides and freezes. Not on the HS path (it only loads the sense leaf)."
  },
