### FILE: tests/regression/t3_nand_io/answer_key_README.md
<!-- sha256=e01764bd29d2c7ef530f1dacd34b96861a1b8075682dbf216a34e3fc60745b9b newline=1 -->
`````markdown
# Answer key format

`nand_io_full.json` is the designer's ground truth for `nand_io_full.sp`, the full NAND flash IO block. Its top cell is `nf_io_top`. The format is the same as the sub-block keys in `material/answer_key`. The class vocabulary is extended as described below.

## Top-level fields

- `netlist`: the netlist file.
- `top`: the top cell. It is a `.subckt`, and nothing instantiates it.
- `supplies`, `grounds`: the supply and ground port names. They are `vdd`/`vccq` and `vss`/`vssq`.
- `ports`: one entry per top-cell port. A bus is written as `name<MSB:LSB>`; the 153 pins are grouped into 49 entries. Each entry has:
  - `class`: one of the port classes below.
  - `function`: a one-line description.
- `cells`: an entry for **every** subcircuit in the netlist (92). That covers all hierarchical cells and all leaf cells, whether or not they are on the high-speed path.

## Port classes

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `hs_data_in` / `hs_data_out` / `hs_data_io` | High-speed (bit-rate) data. `dq<7:0>` is `hs_data_io` because the pad is bidirectional. |
| `clock_in` / `clock_out` | Clocks and strobes. `dqs`/`dqsb` are bidirectional strobe pads and are classed `clock_in`; their function text says they are also driven on reads. `cal_clk` is a slow calibration clock. |
| `word_rate_data` | Core-side parallel data: `din<31:0>` (1:4 deser output) and `dout_e/o<7:0>` (serializer inputs). |
| `important_control` | Mode, enable and strength controls that change the high-speed behaviour (`rx_mode_um`, `dq_oe`, `odt_code`, ...). |
| `general_control` | Trims, resets and overrides (`dq_dskw`, `dqs_dly`, `sr_code`, `pu_ovr`, ...). |
| `command` | Command-decoder strobes that start an operation: `zq_start`, `dcc_train`. |
| `status_out` | Read-back and status: `zq_done`, `zq_pu_code`, `zq_pd_code`, `dcc_lock`, `dcc_code`. |
| `test_digital` | `tm_rxobs`, `rx_obs`. |
| `reference` | Reference voltage or resistor pins: `vref_ext`, `zq`. |
| `bias` | Bias current: `ibias`. |
| `power` | Supplies and grounds. |
| `slow_signal` | Defined for completeness; not used at the top. |

## Per-cell fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `role` | What the block is. |
| `on_high_speed_path` | `true` if the cell carries the high-speed data or clock/strobe signal in series: the mission data path, the strobe/clock distribution, the pad pass-through, the DCA in the RE path. Static control, bias, calibration (DCC detector/comparator/counter, ZQ), termination, test and rail-ESD cells are `false`. A generic library cell is `true` if any instance of it sits on such a path. |
| `inverting` | The polarity from the main input to the main output. It is `null` for cells with several outputs or several functions (for example the bidirectional slices), or with no single in→out path. |
| `children` | Subcircuit instances only. MOS, R and C devices are not listed. An iterated instance is listed once under its Virtuoso iterated name (`XI7<7:0>`), which stands for the expanded `XI7<7>` … `XI7<0>`. |
| `signal_flow` | A list of `[source, destination, net, net_class]` entries. It gives the main paths and is not an exhaustive connectivity dump. Bidirectional pads appear in both directions. |
| `controls` | Maps a control net (or bus `MSB:LSB`) to what it sets. |
| `notes` | Feedback loops, unused outputs, intentional asymmetry, mode muxes, and so on. |

## `signal_flow` endpoint syntax

- `PORT.<pin>` is a pin of the cell itself.
- `<inst>.<pin>` is a pin of a child instance, using the pin name from that child's `.subckt` line.
  - A range of an iterated instance is allowed (`XI7<7:0>.de`), including a stepped range (`XI0<14:0:2>.z`).
  - So is a bus pin (`XI7<7:0>.rd<3:0>`, whose net is the matching bus `din<31:0>`: `XI7<7>.rd<3>` maps to `din<31>`, …, `XI7<0>.rd<0>` maps to `din<0>`).
  - When a bus pin of an iterated range lists a narrower net (`XI7<7:0>.pu_en<4:0>` with `pu_en_d<4:0>`), every instance connects to that same bus.
- `<MOS>.<d|g|s|b>` is a MOS terminal.
- A bare device name (`RR0`, or an iterated group `RR1<30:0>`) is a passive R or C, or a ladder, where the terminal does not matter.
- Net names follow the netlist.
  - Buses use `<MSB:LSB>`.
  - A stepped range is `<start:stop:step>`, for example `t<31:1:2>` for the odd taps.

## `net_class` values

`net_class` is the direction-free form of the port classes. The values are:
- `hs_data`
- `clock`
- `word_rate_data`
- `important_control`
- `general_control`
- `command`
- `status`
- `reference` (VREF nodes, ladder taps, ZQ pin and replica nodes)
- `bias` (bias currents, self-bias and slew-bias nodes)
- `slow_signal` (loop-internal analog/digital nodes: detector outputs, comparator outputs, SAR phases)
- `test_digital`
- `power`

## Conventions

- Iterated instances and buses are written MSB first.
- In a bit slice, `rd<0>` / `din<4n>` is the first UI of the 4-UI word.
- Device multiplicity (`m=`) on subcircuit instances is shown in the netlist and mentioned in `role` and `notes`. The flattened MOS count (6833) counts device instances and ignores `m`; the sum of `m` is 7407.

## Checks run on this file (`scripts/check_key.py`)

- The `ports` entries expand to exactly the 153 pins of `nf_io_top`, and every class is from the list above.
- Every subcircuit has an entry, and every entry names a subcircuit.
- Every child list matches the netlist exactly, including iterated instances.
- Every endpoint names an existing instance or device and an existing pin.
- Every net exists in its cell.
- Every endpoint, scalar or range, really connects to the net named for it (bit by bit for ranges).
- Every `controls` key is a net of the cell.
`````

### FILE: tests/regression/t3_nand_io/intent.md
<!-- sha256=0def8db02ea707671740d004480714513f192fcb34bdc66b6f95c0218c09982e newline=1 -->
`````markdown
# NAND flash IO, full block: designer's note

`nand_io_full.sp` is a Virtuoso `hspiceD` export of one top cell, **`nf_io_top`**. It is the complete DDR (Toggle/ONFI-style) byte IO of a NAND die: 8 DQ pins, DQS/DQSB, RE/nRE, ZQ and VREF.

The file is self-contained. It has placeholder `.MODEL` cards and no `.include`. The top cell is itself a `.subckt`, and nothing instantiates it.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Subcircuits | 92 |
| Hierarchy depth | 6 levels (for example `nf_io_top` / `io_dq_slice` / `tx_dq_slice` / `tx_predrv` / `tx_predrv_leg` / `nand2_q`) |
| Cells mixing devices and instances | 22 (`rx_saff`, `tx_dca`, `tx_ser2`, `tx_predrv_leg`, `rx_vref_gen`, `zq_cal`, `io_pad_bidir`, ...) |
| Flattened MOS (instances) | 6833 (sum of `m=`: 7407) |
| Flattened R / C | 279 / 118 |
| Device lines in the file | 494 X, 292 M, 67 R, 36 C |

## Conventions

**Supplies:**
- `vdd` is the core supply, about 1.0 V. `vccq` is the IO supply, 1.2 V.
- The grounds are `vss` (core) and `vssq` (IO).
- `vss` and `vssq` are coupled only through the back-to-back ESD devices in `esd_rail`.

**Device flavours:**
- `nch`/`pch` are core devices.
- `nch_lvt`/`pch_lvt` are low-Vt core devices, used in the high-speed clock and data cells.
- `nch_hv`/`pch_hv` are thick-oxide IO devices. They are used everywhere on VCCQ and on every pad-facing gate.
- No core device touches `vccq`/`vssq`. Every NMOS bulk is on `vss`/`vssq` and every PMOS bulk on `vdd`/`vccq`; the structure check confirms both.

**Naming:**
- Instances are `XI<n>`. MOS devices are `MM<n>`, with a few named devices: `MMtail`, `MMclamp`, `MMN1`...
- Iterated instances are expanded MSB first (`XI7<7>` ... `XI7<0>`).
- Buses are MSB first (`code<4:0>`).
- Internal nets mix Virtuoso `net0xx` names with meaningful names.

**Libraries** (shown in the `** Library name:` comments):
- `NFIO_STD`: gates, flops, level shifters, clock buffers.
- `NFIO_RX`: receive path.
- `NFIO_TX`: transmit and RE clock path.
- `NFIO_CAL`: DCC and ZQ.
- `NFIO_ESD`: ESD.
- `NFIO_IO`: pad cells, ODT, control and bias hubs, slices, top.

## Top-level pins of `nf_io_top`

### High-speed pads (bidirectional, with ESD)

| Pin | Function |
|---|---|
| `dq<7:0>` | **High-speed data in/out.** Write data comes in to the Rx slices. Read data goes out from the Tx slices on the same pad. |
| `dqs`, `dqsb` | **Strobe, bidirectional.** On writes it is an input: a center-aligned strobe whose two edges sample DQ (`dqsb` is replaced by VREF in single-ended mode). On reads it is driven as an output strobe, generated from RE through a DQ-identical Tx slice, so it is edge-aligned to DQ. |
| `re`, `reb` | **Clock input**, RE/nRE (differential read enable; `reb` is replaced by VREF in single-ended mode). It is the read clock for all outputs. |

### Core-side data and clocks

| Pin | Function |
|---|---|
| `din<31:0>` | **Word-rate data out** to the core: 1:4 deserialized write data. `din<4n+3:4n>` holds DQ<n> UI3..UI0, so `din<4n>` is the first UI. All 4 bits of a word update together, once per DQS/2 period. |
| `din_clk` | **Clock out**: DQS/2 word clock (`div_p` buffered). The core captures `din` on its rising edge, which falls in the middle of the stable window. |
| `dout_e<7:0>`, `dout_o<7:0>` | **Word-rate data in** from the core: even and odd read data per DQ. The even bit is sent while the RE-derived clock is high, the odd bit while it is low. |
| `rclk_core` | **Clock out**: RE-derived clock (core tap of the Tx tree) that launches `dout_e`/`dout_o` and `dqs_burst`. |
| `cal_clk` | **Slow clock in** (about 10 MHz, from the core oscillator). It clocks the ZQ SAR and counter and the DCC comparator and counter. It is not a high-speed clock. |

### Reference and bias

| Pin | Function |
|---|---|
| `vref_ext` | Reference: external VREFQ pad (with ESD), used when `vref_int_en=0`. |
| `zq` | Reference: ZQ pad to the external RZQ, 300 Ω to VSSQ. Primary ESD only, with no series R. |
| `ibias` | Bias: about 10 µA from the bandgap. It is mirrored to the ZQ comparators (sink) and the VREF buffer (source). |

Internal reference and bias nets:
- `vref_rx` (VREFQ) is shared by the 8 DQ receivers, the single-ended DQS reference and the single-ended RE reference.
- `vref_zq` (VCCQ/2) is inside `zq_cal`.
- `vbp_sr`/`vbn_sr` are the pre-driver slew bias.
- `ib_zq` and `ib_vref` are the mirrored bias currents.

### Commands, status, test

| Pin | Class | Function |
|---|---|---|
| `zq_start` | command | One `cal_clk` pulse that starts the pull-up SAR (ZQ calibration command). |
| `dcc_train` | command | DCC training. 1 = run the duty loop while the host toggles RE. 0 = hold the code, clear the lock, gate off the detector and update clock. |
| `zq_done` | status out | Pull-up SAR finished. It also starts PD tracking. |
| `zq_pu_code<4:0>`, `zq_pd_code<4:0>` | status out | Read back the ZQ result. The same nets drive the driver strength internally. |
| `dcc_lock` | status out | DCC locked after two dither events. It also freezes the code. |
| `dcc_code<4:0>` | status out | Current DCC code (offset binary, 10000 neutral). |
| `tm_rxobs` / `rx_obs` | test | Observe `div_p` (DQS/2) on `rx_obs`. |

### Control codes and what they control

| Pin | Controls |
|---|---|
| `rx_en` | Rx power: DQ/DQS receivers (Bazes tails), strobe trees and chains, the VREF DAC qualifier, the observe gate. |
| `rx_mode_um` | **Rx path select.** 0 = matched: DQ goes through `dq_match_dly` and DQS through the 1→3→9 H-trees. 1 = unmatched: DQ goes direct and DQS through the 9-stage repeater chain, whose tap *n* drives DQ<n>. The inactive network is clock-gated (`en_m`/`en_u`; `selub` gates the DQ replica). |
| `dqs_se` | Single-ended DQS (DQS vs VREF) vs differential DQS/DQSB. |
| `vref_int_en` | Internal VREF DAC (ladder + OTA, powered only when selected) vs `vref_ext`. |
| `vref_code<4:0>` | Internal VREF tap, about 34.5 %…71.4 % of VCCQ in about 1.2 % steps. |
| `dqs_dly<2:0>` | Cap-load delay trim on both Rx strobe phases. |
| `dq_dskw<23:0>` | Per-bit Rx DQ deskew, 3 bits per bit (`dq_dskw<3n+2:3n>` for DQ<n>), for training in unmatched mode. |
| `rx_rst_n` | Resets the DQS/2 divider. The release point sets the deser word alignment. |
| `tx_en` | RE receiver enable. |
| `re_se` | Single-ended RE vs differential RE/nRE. |
| `dq_oe` | DQ driver enable. 0 = every PU and PD leg off (Hi-Z). 1 also forces the DQ-group ODT off. |
| `dqs_oe` | DQS/DQSB driver enable (preamble to postamble). 1 also forces the DQS-group ODT off. |
| `dqs_burst` | 1 = DQS/DQSB toggle with RE. 0 = DQS low and DQSB high (preamble/postamble). It is retimed in the slices. |
| `sr_code<1:0>` | Output slew: starving current of the pre-driver final stages. |
| `odt_en`, `odt_code<2:0>` | Termination on DQ/DQS/DQSB: about 300/150/100/75/60/50/43 Ω Thevenin for codes 1..7. It is effective only while that pin group is not driving. |
| `zq_en`, `zq_rst_n` | ZQ analog enable (VREF divider, comparators, replica gates, PD tracking). The reset gives SAR code 0 and PD counter 10000. |
| `drv_ovr_en`, `pu_ovr<4:0>`, `pd_ovr<4:0>` | Driver strength source. 0 = ZQ codes, 1 = override codes (bring-up/test). |
| `dcc_rst_n` | Resets the DCC code to 10000. |

## Signal flow and sub-blocks

### Rx (write data in)

1. **Pad.** `dq<n>` → `io_dq_slice/XI0 io_pad_bidir`. This is GDPMOS/GGNMOS primary protection, then 200 Ω + GGNMOS secondary protection, giving `pad_rx`.
2. **Front end.** `rx_dq_slice`: always-on input TG `rx_tg_q` → `rx_amp_bz` (Bazes self-biased receiver on VCCQ, DQ vs `vref_rx`) → `rx_ls_dn` (VCCQ→VDD) → `dly_trim3` (deskew).
3. **Path select.** `dq_match_dly` (a replica of the strobe `ckgate` + root/branch/leaf `ckbuf`), then three `mux2_hs` cells select data, rise strobe and fall strobe for matched or unmatched mode.
4. **Sampling.** `rx_samp_pair` holds two StrongARM `rx_saff`: rise samples on the true strobe, fall samples on the complement strobe.
5. **Deserialization.** `rx_deser4`: the rise sample is retimed onto the fall strobe. UI0/UI1 are captured on `div_p`. UI2/UI3 are captured on `div_n` and UI0/UI1 re-registered on `div_n`, so the 4-bit word changes once per word.
6. **Strobe path.** `rx_dqs_path` takes `dqs_rx`/`dqsb_rx` from the two `io_dqs_slice` pad cells:
   - An always-on DQS TG, plus DQSB/VREF select TGs.
   - Two identical `rx_amp_bz` with swapped inputs make the true and complement strobes, with equal latency.
   - Then `rx_ls_dn`, `dly_trim3` and `ckgate`.
   - Then the matched `rx_dqs_tree` ×2 and the unmatched `rx_rpt_chain` ×2.
7. **Word clock.** `rx_ckdiv_slice`: a mode mux on leaf/tap 8 of the true strobe, then the `dffr_tg` toggle divider giving `div_p`/`div_n`, then the `din_clk` driver.

**Matching by construction:** the DQ pad cell, TG, receiver, level shifter, trim, clock gate, buffers and mux are the same cells as on the strobe side. In matched mode the strobe-to-data delay difference cancels.

### Tx (read data out)

1. **RE input.** RE/nRE pads (`io_pad_in`) → `re_clk_path`.
2. **Receiver.** `tx_re_rx`: TGs, Bazes receiver, a dummy swapped receiver for input-load symmetry, `rx_ls_dn`.
3. **Duty adjust.** `tx_ckbuf_dca`: `ckbuf` → **`tx_dca`** (the DCC actuator) → `ckbuf_x8`.
4. **Distribution.** `tx_rpt_chain` (4 repeaters + RC wire) → `tx_cktree`:
   - Root, 2 branches of 6 leaves each.
   - `lf<7:0>` go to the DQ slices, `lf<8>` to DQS, `lf<9>` to DQSB.
   - A core tap feeds `tx_rpt` → `rclk_core`.
   - **`lf_dcc` = `ck_dcc`** is the DCC sense leaf, beside the DQS leaves.
5. **Per pin `tx_dq_slice`:**
   - `ck_split` (ck/ckb).
   - `tx_ser2`: even and odd DFFs on ck falling, a half-cycle latch on the odd path, and a TG mux. ck high sends even, ck low sends odd.
   - `ls_up_hs` (VDD→VCCQ).
   - `tx_predrv`: 5 × `tx_predrv_leg` (NAND/NOR with enables, then a current-starved final stage) → `pg<4:0>`/`ng<4:0>`.
6. **Main driver.** The pad cell's `tx_out_drv`: 5 × `tx_drv_unit` with m = 16/8/4/2/1. Each unit is pch_hv 8 µm + 300 Ω up and nch_hv 4 µm + 300 Ω down.
7. **DQS/DQSB.** These use the same `tx_dq_slice` and `io_pad_bidir` (`io_dqs_slice`). The constant patterns from `tx_ctrl` are DQS e=`dqs_burst`, o=0 and DQSB e=~`dqs_burst`, o=1.

### DCC loop (closed, on the RE → repeater → driver clock path)

The loop runs: `dcc_code` → `tx_dca` → RPT chain → tree → `ck_dcc` → `dcc_ctrl`.

Inside `dcc_ctrl`:
- `dcc_det`: a gated clock and its complement drive matched 2-pole RC filters (50 k/0.5 p, 50 k/0.25 p), giving `vp`≈D·VDD and `vn`≈(1−D)·VDD.
- `sa_cmp`: StrongARM comparator on `upd_clk` = `cal_clk` & `dcc_train`.
- `updn_cnt5`: up/down counter, reset to 10000.
- `dcc_lock_det`.
- The counter output `dcc_code` feeds back to `tx_dca`.

**Polarity:** duty > 50 % → `up`=1 → code counts up → the DCA pull-up legs speed the falling output edge → shorter high phase.

**Code map:** 1xxxx shortens the high phase by `code<3:0>` units. 0xxxx lengthens it by `~code<3:0>` units. 10000 and 01111 are both neutral, so the code is monotonic with one duplicate step.

**Lock:** after two valid decision reversals (the first decision after training starts is ignored), `dcc_lock`=1 drives the counter `hold` and freezes the code.

### ZQ calibration (`zq_cal`) → driver strength

**Pull-up loop:**
- `zq_vref` gives VCCQ/2.
- `zq_pu_rep` holds the replica PU legs on the ZQ pin, against RZQ.
- `zq_cmp` (static comparator + `ls_dn`) feeds `zq_sar5`, a 5-step SAR. A comparator 1 means ZQ is above VREF, so the PU is too strong and the trial bit is cleared. The result is `pu_code`.

**Pull-down loop:**
- `zq_pd_rep` is an internal PU copy on top of the PD replica legs, at node `npd`.
- `zq_cmp` feeds `updn_cnt5`, which tracks after `zq_done` and dithers ±1 LSB. The result is `pd_code`.

**Scaling:** the replica unit is 1/8 of the driver unit (1 µm + 2.4 kΩ vs 8 µm + 300 Ω). Matching RZQ = 300 Ω therefore sets the drivers to about 37.5 Ω.

**Code path to the drivers:**
1. `zq_cal.pu_code/pd_code` → `io_ctrl/drv_code_mux` (ZQ or override).
2. → `tx_ctrl`: level shift, then gate with `dq_oe` (DQ group) and `dqs_oe` (DQS group). This gives `pu_en_d/s<4:0>` (active-high PU enables) and `pd_dis_d/s<4:0>` (active-high PD disables).
3. → the per-leg pre-drivers of every DQ and DQS/DQSB slice.

### ESD and ODT

- **`io_pad_bidir`** (DQ ×8, DQS, DQSB) contains:
  - `esd_io_pad`: primary GDPMOS/GGNMOS plus a 200 Ω/GGNMOS secondary on the receiver side.
  - The main driver.
  - `odt_leg_pin`: 3 binary center-tapped PU/PD pairs.
  - A 0.2 pF pad cap.
- **`io_pad_in`** (RE, nRE, VREF_EXT): `esd_io_pad` and a pad cap.
- **ZQ:** `esd_prim`, primary only.
- **`esd_rail`:** RC-triggered clamps VCCQ-VSSQ and VDD-VSS, and `esd_b2b` VSS-VSSQ.
- **`odt_ctrl`** (in `io_ctrl`) makes separate gate buses for the DQ group and the DQS group: `odt_en & ~dq_oe` and `odt_en & ~dqs_oe`. The termination therefore never fights the driver it shares a pad with.

### Control and bias hubs (static)

- **`io_ctrl`** = `rx_ctrl` + `drv_code_mux` + `tx_ctrl` + `odt_ctrl`. All inputs are VDD-domain register/command bits. The `_q` outputs and the leg/ODT gate buses are VCCQ.
- **`io_bias`** = `ib_dist` + `tx_sr_bias` + `rx_vref_gen` (32-tap ladder, `vref_mux32` TG tree, `vref_buf_ota`, ext/int `amux2_q`, decap).

## What is and is not on the high-speed path

**On the path (in series with data or strobe/clock):**
- Rx: pad cells (passive pass-through), `rx_dq_slice` and below, `rx_dqs_path`, `rx_dqs_tree`, `rx_rpt_chain`, `rx_ckdiv_slice`.
- Tx: `re_clk_path` and below (including `tx_dca`), `tx_dq_slice` and below, `tx_out_drv`.
- Shared library cells: the HS library cells, and `dffr_tg`/`nand2_x1`/`nor2_x1` inside the divider.

**Not on the path:**
- Control: `io_ctrl` (`rx_ctrl`, `tx_ctrl`, `odt_ctrl`, `drv_code_mux`, `mux2_x1`, `ls_up`, `inv_x2`, `tie_hilo`).
- Bias and reference: `io_bias` (`ib_dist`, `tx_sr_bias`, `rx_vref_gen`, `vref_mux32`, `vref_buf_ota`, `amux2_q`).
- Calibration: `zq_cal` and all its children, and `dcc_ctrl` (`dcc_det`, `sa_cmp`, `updn_cnt5`, `dcc_lock_det`; it only loads the sense leaf).
- Termination and rail ESD: `odt_leg_pin` (a shunt load), `esd_rail`, `esd_rc_clamp`, `esd_b2b`, `esd_prim`.
- Test: `rx_obs_buf`.

**Signal categories:**
- Word-rate digital: `din<31:0>`, `dout_e/o<7:0>`, and inside the cells `p0/p1/rd` of the deser and `de/do/qe/qo` of the serializer.
- Slow loop-internal signals: `vp/vn/up`, `cmp_pu/cmp_pd`, SAR phase.

## Intentional asymmetries and unused nets

- **Dummy loads (unused outputs):**
  - `ckc_m<8>` and `ckc_u<8>`: the complement-strobe leaf/tap 8.
  - `tx_re_rx/net011`: the dummy receiver output.
  - `dcc_det/net012`.
- **Unused flop `qb` outputs:** the sampler `qb`s (`rx_samp_pair/net07`, `net08`), `zq_sar5 phb/codeb/doneb`, `updn_cnt5 cqb/net012`, `dcc_lock_det/net010`, `net011`, and the DCC comparator `qb` (`dcc_ctrl/net011`).
- **Unused level-shifter complements:** in `tx_ctrl`, `odt_ctrl`, `tx_sr_bias` and `zq_gate_drv`.
- **Unused gate-driver outputs:** `zq_cal pu_g<4:0>` and `pd_gb<4:0>`.
- **Other asymmetries:**
  - The ratioed `ls_up_hs` has unequal rise/fall delays.
  - The DCA's rise/fall asymmetry is the correction mechanism.
  - The `div_n` buffer is one inverter later than `div_p`. This is tolerated, because the deser window is a full DQS period.
- **Tie-offs:**
  - `dcc_lock_det/XI2` has its D tied to `vdd` (a valid flag).
  - The ZQ PD counter `hold` is tied to `vss`.

## Integration changes vs. the separate sub-block netlists

- The main driver legs moved from `tx_dq_slice` into the shared pad cell. The pad cap moved from `tx_out_drv` to `io_pad_bidir`.
- The DCC now lives in the RE path: the standalone `dcc_dca` was dropped and `tx_dca` is used. The detector now senses tree leaf `lf_dcc`, which was the dummy leaf. The local monitor tap was removed. A lock detector was added.
- `rx_deser4` now has 6 flops, so all 4 output bits update together. In the old version half the word changed on the core capture edge.
- The ZQ replica legs were rescaled to 1/8 of the driver unit, so the calibrated code gives the right driver impedance.
- `ib_dist` now also sources the VREF buffer bias.
- ODT now has per-group auto-off.
- The SE RE reference is the shared `vref_rx`.
- `wire_rc` was split into `wire_rc_rx`/`wire_rc_tx` (different RC), and duplicate library cells were merged.

## Checks run (scripts in `scripts/`)

**`check_netlist.py`:** all 92 subckts are defined before use and used, there is exactly one top, and the pin counts match. MOS have 4 terminals, a known model and W/L. The bulk/domain rules hold. No pin is unconnected inside its cell. Every single-connection net is in the intentional list above.

**`check_logic.py`:** a unit-delay switch-level simulation (`swsim.py`) of the netlist's own transistors. It passed 994 checks:
- Every standard gate and level shifter.
- Every flop and latch.
- `tx_dca` decode and polarity for all 32 codes.
- Tree and chain polarity.
- The DQS-slice serializer through the pad: even/odd order, Hi-Z, partial strength, ODT.
- Samplers + 6-flop deser + divider, with words checked in UI order.
- `updn_cnt5`: count, saturate, hold, reset.
- `zq_sar5` with a behavioural comparator: all 32 targets in 5 steps.
- The closed DCC loop with a behavioural duty model: it locks within ±1 LSB from both sides, freezes, and releases on `dcc_train`=0.
- `io_ctrl` decode on random vectors.

**Not simulated:** the analog cells (Bazes receivers, OTA, ZQ comparators, ESD, RC detector) were checked by inspection only.

**`check_key.py`:** validates the answer key against the netlist.
`````

`````json
  "fcr_bbx": {
   "role": "Alexander (bang-bang) phase detector with data retiming: data flops s0/s1 on ck falling, edge flop e0 on ck rising then e1 on ck falling, up = e1 XOR s0, dn = s1 XOR e1",
   "on_high_speed_path": true,
   "inverting": null,
   "children": [

     "cell": "fcd_dff",
     "role": "s0 = D[k] (ck falling: ck pin = ckb)"

     "role": "dn = D[k-1] XOR E: edge sample equals the later bit -> clock late"

    ]
   ],
   "controls": {},
   "notes": "LOOK-ALIKE: DFFs followed by XORs resemble a BIST/PRBS checker or a plain sampler bank. Tell-tales: the two inputs are data and edge samples of the same signal taken half a UI apart, the flops run on both clock edges (ck pin swapped on X0/X1/X3), there is no pattern generator, LFSR feedback or error counter, and the XOR outputs go to a vote + up/down counter that steers the interpolator (a loop). up and dn are both 1 only on a non-transition with an edge mismatch; the vote cancels that. s0/s1 are also the first two deserializer stages (mission data), hence on_high_speed_path. s0b, s1b, e0b, e1b unused."
  },
`````

### FILE: tests/regression/t4_fwdclk/answer_key_README.md
<!-- sha256=a1492ae038eba3334e93860a1d8f9a26f43047b24a163ffb8888b8cec074a146 newline=1 -->
`````markdown
# Answer key format

`netlist_g.json` is the designer's ground truth for `netlist_g.sp`, a forwarded-clock serial-link IO. Its top cell is `fcl_link_top`. The format is the same as the iter3 key (`nand_io_full.json`). This key adds a few fields and classes, all defined below.

## Top-level fields

- `netlist`: the netlist file.
- `top`: the top cell. It is a `.subckt`, and nothing instantiates it.
- `supplies`, `grounds`: the supply and ground **ports** of the top: `avdd`/`vddq` and `avss`/`vssq`.
- `globals` (new): supplies that are `.global` nets and not pins: `vddd`/`vssd`. The FCL_STD cells and the digital cells built from them have no supply pins. The analog, CML, ESD and pad cells take `avdd`/`avss` or `vddq`/`vssq` as pins.
- `ports`: one entry per top-cell port. A bus is written `name[MSB:LSB]`. The 111 pins are grouped into 28 entries. Each entry has:
  - `class`: one of the port classes below.
  - `function`: a one-line description.
- `cells`: an entry for **every** subcircuit in the netlist (55). That covers all hierarchical cells and all leaf cells, whether or not they are on the high-speed path.

## Port classes

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `hs_data_in` / `hs_data_out` / `hs_data_io` | Bit-rate data. `rx_p/rx_n[3:0]` are inputs and `tx_p/tx_n` are outputs. `hs_data_io` is not used here. |
| `clock_in` / `clock_out` | Clocks and strobes. `fck_p/fck_n` is the forwarded clock. `cstb_pad` is the slow command strobe; its function text says it is not a high-speed clock. `rx_wck[3:0]` and `tx_wck` are word clocks. |
| `word_rate_data` | Core-side parallel data: `rxd[31:0]` (1:8 deser outputs) and `txd[7:0]` (serializer input). |
| `important_control` | Controls that change high-speed behaviour: the Tx FFE weights `txffe_pre/main/post`. |
| `general_control` | Resets: `rst_n`, `dll_rst_n`. |
| `command` | Defined for completeness; not used at the top. |
| `status_out` | Read-back: `rx_pic[19:0]` (CDR codes) and `cmd_q[3:0]` (command register). |
| `test_digital` | `ro_div`, `ro_cnt[5:0]`, `fc_rst_n`. |
| `test_analog` (new) | Analog observation pin: `dll_vmon`, the DLL control voltage through 20 k. |
| `reference` | Defined for completeness; not used at the top. The termination common mode is generated inside. |
| `bias` | Bias current: `ibias`. |
| `power` | Supplies and grounds. |
| `slow_signal` | The slow single-ended CMOS command pads `cmd_pad[3:0]`. |

## Per-cell fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `role` | What the block is. |
| `on_high_speed_path` | `true` if the cell carries bit-rate data or a high-speed clock in series: the receive data path, the DLL and phase distribution, the phase interpolator and samplers, the deserializer, the Johnson word-clock divider, the serializer, FFE and driver. Loop-control cells are `false`: PFD, charge pump, loop filter, vote and accumulator. So are bias, termination, ESD, the test oscillator and the slow pads. A generic library cell is `true` if any instance of it sits on such a path. One subtle case: `fcr_bbx` (the Alexander PD) is `true`, because its two data-retime flops are also the first two deserializer stages. |
| `inverting` | The polarity from the main input to the main output. It may be a single value or an object. **Extended:** <ul><li>`true`/`false` for a cell with one main output.</li><li>An object `{output_pin: true/false}` for a cell with several main outputs, such as a differential pair: `{"outp": false, "outn": true}` means `outp` follows the true input.</li><li>`null` when there is no single in→out polarity: several functions, a loop, a passive network, or an enable-only path.</li></ul> |
| `children` | Subcircuit instances only. MOS, R and C devices are not listed. An iterated instance is listed once under its iterated name (`X0[7:0]`), which stands for `X0[7]` … `X0[0]`. |
| `signal_flow` | A list of `[source, destination, net, net_class]` entries. It gives the main paths and is not an exhaustive connectivity dump. |
| `controls` | Maps a control net (or bus `[MSB:LSB]`, or a `p/n` pair such as `ck/ckb`) to what it sets. |
| `notes` | Feedback loops, unused outputs, intentional asymmetry, look-alike traps and so on. |

## `signal_flow` endpoint syntax

- `PORT.<pin>` is a pin of the cell itself.
- `<inst>.<pin>` is a pin of a child instance, using the pin name from that child's `.subckt` line.
  - A range of an iterated instance is allowed (`X0[7:2].q`), including a stepped range (`X1[3:1:2].y` = `X1[3]`, `X1[1]`).
  - So is a bus pin of an iterated range. `X2[3:0].rxd[7:0]` with net `rxd[31:0]` maps `X2[3].rxd[7]` to `rxd[31]`, …, `X2[0].rxd[0]` to `rxd[0]`.
  - When the net is narrower than the expanded endpoint, every instance connects to that same bus. For example, `X2[3:0].ph[7:0]` with net `ph[7:0]` means all four lanes get `ph[7:0]`.
- `<MOS>.<d|g|s|b>` is a MOS terminal.
- A bare device name (`R0`, `C1`) is a passive R or C, where the terminal does not matter.
- Net names follow the netlist:
  - Buses use `[MSB:LSB]`. An ascending range (`rxd[0:7]`) lists bits in that order and is used when the bit order reverses.
  - A stepped range is `[start:stop:step]`, for example `ph[7:1:2]` for the odd phases.

## `net_class` values

`net_class` is the direction-free form of the port classes, plus three new classes for loops. The values are:
- `hs_data`
- `clock`: includes the DLL phases, PI output, CMOS sampling clocks, word clocks, the Johnson load pulse `ld`, and the slow strobe.
- `word_rate_data`
- `important_control`
- `general_control`
- `command`
- `status`
- `reference`: the termination common mode `vcm`.
- `bias`: bias currents and gate voltages, tail nodes, charge-pump bias.
- `slow_signal`: slow pad signals before the command register.
- `test_digital`
- `test_analog` (new)
- `power`: ESD and clamp nodes.
- `loop_control` (new): analog loop control voltages. These are the DLL `vctl` (charge pump → loop filter → delay-line NMOS starve gates) and `vcp` (the PMOS starve bias derived from `vctl`). They keep this class where the same nodes bias the replica ring oscillator.
- `loop_error` (new): phase-error signals inside a loop. These are the PFD `up/dn/upb/dnb` and its reset nodes, the Alexander-PD `up/dn`, the vote outputs `vub/vdb`, and the decoded count enables `u/d`.
- `pi_code` (new): the digital CDR state that steers the interpolator. It covers the accumulator code and carries, `code[4:2]` as the phase-pair select (`k`, `kb`), and `code[1:0]`/`codeb[1:0]` as the interpolator tail weights `w`/`wb`. At the lane port the same code is shown as `status` for the read-back path.

Classes follow what a signal does, not its name. For example, `ld` is a capture strobe (`clock`), not data. `vcn` in `fct_cs5` is the DLL control voltage (`loop_control`), even though it only biases the oscillator there.

## Conventions

- Iterated instances and buses are written MSB first, except where an ascending range marks a bit-order reversal.
- In a lane word, `rxd[8n]` is the oldest bit, the first UI of the word. In the Tx, `txd[0]` is sent first.
- Phases are named by phase, not by stage: `ph[k]` / `pho[k]` is at k × 45°.
- Device multiplicity (`m=`) on instances (DAC legs, clock drivers) and on devices is shown in the netlist and mentioned in `role` and `notes`.
  - The flattened MOS count (3992) counts device instances and ignores `m`.
  - The sum of `m` is 4687.
- The netlist uses `.param` values (W/L names and expressions), subckt default parameters (`rl=` on the CML cells) and instance overrides (`rl=450`, `rl=420`).

## Checks run on this file (`scripts/check_key.py`)

- The `ports` entries expand to exactly the 111 pins of `fcl_link_top`, every class is from the lists above, and every port has a function.
- `globals` are declared `.global` in the netlist.
- Every subcircuit has an entry, and every entry names a subcircuit.
- Every child list matches the netlist exactly, including iterated instances, and every child has a role.
- Every endpoint names an existing instance or device and an existing pin.
- Every net exists in its cell.
- Every endpoint, scalar or range, really connects to the net named for it, bit by bit for ranges.
- Every `controls` key is a net of the cell.
- `inverting` is a bool, `null`, or an object whose keys are pins of the cell.
- A mutation test (wrong net, wrong pin, reversed bus, missing child, bad class, dropped port) was run once by hand, and the checker rejected each mutation.
`````

### FILE: tests/regression/t4_fwdclk/intent.md
<!-- sha256=411fbcecca86f68a076bad9009a49587ad5f36609f5254caecc5488e7c597efe newline=1 -->
`````markdown
# netlist_g.sp: designer's note (for the verifier only)

Top cell `fcl_link_top`, a forwarded-clock serial-link IO. There are 55 subckts, the hierarchy is 6 levels deep, and the flattened netlist has 3992 MOS (sum of m = 4687), 74 R and 20 C. The top has 111 pins.

## 1. Domains and conventions

| Domain | Rails | How they reach the cells |
|---|---|---|
| Core digital | `vddd` / `vssd` | `.global`, never a pin. All FCL_STD cells and the digital blocks use these nets directly, and so do the output stage of `fca_c2c`, the local clock inverters of `fca_pfd` and the level-down inverter in `fcs_inrx`. |
| Analog / CML | `avdd` / `avss` | Pins on every analog cell: CML, DLL delay line, charge pump, PI core, Tx driver, RO, ESD. |
| Slow pad IO | `vddq` / `vssq` | Pins. Thick-oxide devices (`nch_hv`/`pch_hv`) only. |

- Device sizes:
  - Global `.param` values (`wn1`, `wp1`, `lmin`, `lcs`, `wcml`, `wtail` …) and quoted expressions (`W='2*wn1'`).
  - A subckt default parameter `rl=` on the CML cells, overridden per instance (`rl=450` on the clock receiver, `rl=420` on the PI).
  - `m=` on devices and on instances (DAC legs m=1/2/4/8, clock drivers m=2, phase drivers m=2).
- Names:
  - Instances are `X<n>` and iterated instances `X<n>[i]`.
  - Devices are `MN<n>`/`MP<n>`/`R<n>`/`C<n>`.
  - Buses use `[i]`.
- Phases are named by phase angle: `ph[k]` = k × 45°.
- The only comments are the netlister header and the per-cell banners.

## 2. Block list

```
fcl_link_top
 ├ X0  fca_bias        ibias mirror -> vbn_rx, vbn_tx, ib_cp; vcm = 0.75 avdd divider
 ├ X1  fca_fwd         forwarded-clock lane
 │      ├ fca_trm, fca_cmla (rl=450), 2x fca_c2c (true / swapped inputs = complement)
 │      ├ fca_dll
 │      │   ├ fca_dline: 4x fca_dcell + 1 dummy fca_dcell (VCDL, 8 phases)
 │      │   ├ fca_pfd   (2x fcd_dffr, D=vddd, NAND/NOR reset with delay)
 │      │   ├ fca_isw   (charge pump with own bias mirror)
 │      │   ├ fca_lpf   (4k + 20p, 1.5p)
 │      │   └ devices: vctl->vcp converter MN0/MP0, reset PMOS MP1, MOS decap MN1
 │      └ fca_phd       8 inverting drivers, index rotated by 4
 ├ X2[3:0] fcr_lane    data lanes
 │      ├ fca_trm, fca_cmla
 │      ├ fcr_smp       data fca_clff (ckp) + edge fca_clff (ckn) + 2x fca_c2c
 │      ├ fcr_phmix     fcr_phsel (two 8:1 TG trees) + fca_mix2w (PI core)
 │      ├ fca_c2c       PI clock -> CMOS clock for the digital
 │      └ fcr_dig       fcd_ckbuf, fcr_bbx (Alexander PD), fcr_vote, fcr_dsr8, fcr_jdiv8, fcr_acc (5x fcr_ube/fcr_ubo)
 ├ X3  fcx_lane        fcd_ckbuf, fcr_jdiv8, fcx_ser8, fcx_ffe, fcx_drv (9x fca_tleg)
 ├ X4  fct_mon         fct_cs5 (ring of NAND + 4x fct_csi), fcd_ckbuf, fct_rip3 (/8), gate, 2x fct_rip3 (6-bit count)
 ├ X5  fcs_pads        5x fcs_inrx (fce_hv + R + Schmitt + level-down), fcs_creg (4x fcd_dffr)
 ├ X6..X11 fce_lv      ESD on fck_p/n, rx_p/n[3:0], tx_p/n
 └ X12..X14            rail clamps: fce_clmp (avdd/avss), fce_clmp (vddd/vssd), fce_clmphv (vddq/vssq)
```

The deepest path is `fcl_link_top/X2[i]/X5 (fcr_dig)/X5 (fcr_acc)/X5 (fcr_ube)/X0 (fcd_dffr)`.

Ten cells mix devices with instances: `fca_c2c`, `fca_dll`, `fca_pfd`, `fcl_link_top`, `fcr_jdiv8`, `fcr_ube`, `fcr_ubo`, `fcs_inrx`, `fct_cs5`, `fcx_drv`.

## 3. Signal flow

**Forwarded clock**
1. `fck_p/n` arrives with 100 Ω termination to `vcm` and goes through the CML receiver (`fa_p/n`).
2. Two `fca_c2c` make CMOS `ckp` and `ckn`. The second has its inputs swapped.
3. The DLL delay line has four non-inverting differential stages of 45° each. Stage k gives `ph[k]` (true) and `ph[k+4]` (complement): stage 1 gives `ph1`/`ph5`, …, stage 4 gives `ph4`/`ph0`.
4. The PFD compares `ref = ckp` with `fb = ph[0]`. At lock, 4 × delay = T/2, so `ph[0]` = `ckn` delayed by T/2, which lines up with `ckp`.
5. `fca_phd` inverts each phase into `pho[(k+4) mod 8]`, which preserves the phase names.
6. The top net `ph[7:0]` goes to all four lanes, and `ph[0]` also goes to the Tx.

**Data lane** (full-rate; one forwarded-clock period = one UI)
1. `rx_p/n` arrives with termination and goes through `fca_cmla` (`la_p/n`).
2. `fcr_smp` samples twice per UI:
   - The data sampler (CML master-slave) samples at `pck_p` rising.
   - The edge sampler is the same cell with its clocks swapped, so it samples at `pck_n` rising, half a UI later.
   - Each sample is converted to CMOS as `dsam`/`esam`.
3. The PI clock `pck_p/n` comes from `fcr_phmix`:
   - `code[4:2] = k` selects `a = ph[k]` and `b = ph[k+1]`.
   - `code[1:0] = w` sets the tails: A carries 4 − w units and B carries w units.
   - The output phase is (k + w/4) × 45°, in 32 steps over 360°.
4. `fca_c2c` turns `pck` into the CMOS `ck`. `fcd_ckbuf` makes `cka`/`ckab` from it.
5. `fcr_bbx` (Alexander PD):
   - On ck falling, `s0 = D[k]` and `s1 = D[k-1]`.
   - The edge sample is retimed on ck rising (`e0`) and then on ck falling (`e1` = E between D[k-1] and D[k]).
   - `up = e1 ^ s0`: the edge sample equals the earlier bit, so the clock is early and the phase code increases.
   - `dn = s1 ^ e1`: the edge sample equals the later bit, so the clock is late.
6. `fcr_vote` shifts `up`/`dn` on ck falling and outputs `vub`/`vdb`, the active-low majority of the last three decisions.
7. `fcr_acc` is clocked by `wck` rising:
   - It counts up when only up wins, counts down when only dn wins, and holds when both or neither win or when `hold = cmd_q[1]`.
   - The count wraps mod 32.
   - `code` drives the PI. This closes the CDR loop, and the code is read back on `rx_pic`.
8. The deserializer, `fcr_dsr8`:
   - The shift register is `s0`, `s1` (inside the PD) followed by `sr[7:2]`, all on ck falling.
   - `fcr_jdiv8` runs on ck rising. It makes `wck` (÷8, 50 % duty) and `ld = q0 & ~q1`, a one-UI pulse.
   - `ld` opens 8 latches. The latches pass one shift edge and close half a UI later.
   - In `rxd[8n+7:8n]`, the oldest bit is `rxd[8n]`.

**Tx**
1. `ph[0]` goes through `fcd_ckbuf` to `fcr_jdiv8`, which makes `ld` and `tx_wck`.
2. `fcx_ser8` is a shift-load register. `ld = 1` loads `txd[7:0]`; otherwise it shifts toward `sq[0]`. `txd[0]` leaves first, and `so` is the serial stream.
3. `fcx_ffe` makes the taps: `pre = so` (d[n+1]), `main = so` delayed 1 UI (d[n]), `post = so` delayed 2 UI (d[n-1]). Each tap is single-to-differential.
4. In `fcx_drv`, three lvt diff pairs sum into `R0`/`R1` (50 Ω to avdd), which are the termination.
   - The main pair is wired with true polarity. The pre and post pairs are cross-wired, so they subtract.
   - Each tail is a binary DAC of `fca_tleg` instances with m = 1/2/4/8 (main, 4 bits), 1/2 (pre, 2 bits) and 1/2/4 (post, 3 bits). The weights come straight from the register ports `txffe_*`.

**Test ring oscillator**
1. `fct_cs5` is a ring of a current-starved NAND (`en = cmd_q[0]`) and four current-starved inverters, which makes five inverting stages.
   - It is starved by the DLL `vctl`/`vcp`, so it is a replica of the delay-line stage.
2. `fcd_ckbuf` feeds `fct_rip3`, which divides by 8 to give `ro_div`.
3. A NAND gate controlled by `cmd_q[2]` passes the divided clock to two cascaded `fct_rip3`, giving `ro_cnt[5:0]`.
4. `fc_rst_n` clears the divider and the counter.
5. The DLL `vctl` is also brought out through 20 k to `dll_vmon`.

**Slow control**
1. `cmd_pad[3:0]` and `cstb_pad` each go through `fcs_inrx`: `fce_hv` ESD, a 200 Ω series R, a secondary GGNMOS, a 6T Schmitt trigger on vddq, and a thick-oxide inverter to vddd.
2. `fcs_creg` (4× `fcd_dffr`) captures on the strobe's rising edge.
3. The register bits are `cmd_q[0]` RO enable, `cmd_q[1]` CDR hold (all lanes), `cmd_q[2]` count window, and `cmd_q[3]` spare (read back only).
4. `rst_n` clears the register.

**ESD**
- The CML pads use `fce_lv` (GGNMOS + gate-tied PMOS).
- The slow pads use `fce_hv` inside `fcs_inrx`.
- There are three RC-triggered rail clamps (R 60 k, C 2 p, 3 inverters, NMOS m=40).

## 4. Loops

1. **DLL:** `ph[0]` → `fca_pfd` → `upb`/`dn` → `fca_isw` → `vctl` (`fca_lpf`) → `fca_dline` (vcn), and through MN0/MP0 → `vcp` → `fca_dline`. Negative feedback: UP (ref leads) raises `vctl`, which means more current and less delay. `dll_rst_n = 0` pulls `vctl` to avdd (minimum delay), so lock is acquired from the short side.
2. **CDR, per lane:** samplers → `fcr_bbx` → `fcr_vote` → `fcr_acc` → `code` → `fcr_phsel`/`fca_mix2w` → `pck` → samplers and digital clock. The loop is bang-bang, decimated to one update per word.
3. **PFD reset:** `up & dn` → NOR with the external reset → two-inverter delay → the flops' `rb`.
4. **Ring oscillator:** `r4` → NAND → `r0` … → `r4`.
5. **Johnson divider:** `wckb` → `X0.d`, an inverted twisted-ring feedback.
6. **Ripple counters:** each flop's `qb` → its own `d`.
7. **Local feedback that is not a block-level loop:**
   - Schmitt hysteresis (MP2/MN3).
   - Flop and latch keepers.
   - The CML latch regeneration pair.
   - The weak cross-coupled pair in each delay cell.

## 5. Intentional asymmetry

- `fcr_phsel` uses two trees. Tree B has the same structure as tree A but its inputs are rotated by one phase, and `ph[0]` wraps into `X4[3].d1`. There is no select incrementer.
- `a`/`ab` and `b`/`bb` come from different inverter depths, a one-gate skew.
- `fca_phd` is one inverting driver per phase, with the index rotated by 4.
- `fca_dline` has a fifth, dummy delay cell that loads `ph[4]`/`ph[0]`. Its outputs `dmp`/`dmn` are unused.
- `fca_fwd/X3` is the same `fca_c2c` as X2, but its inputs are swapped to make `ckn`.
- `fcr_smp/X1` (edge) is the same `fca_clff` as X0, with `ckp`/`ckn` swapped. In `fca_clff`, the master gets the clocks swapped.
- Clock edges in `fcr_dig` are mixed on purpose. These run on ck falling, through instances with the ck pin wired to `ckab`:
  - the data retime in `fcr_bbx`,
  - the deser shift,
  - the vote.

  These run on ck rising:
  - the edge retime `e0`,
  - the Johnson divider.

  The accumulator runs on `wck`.
- Counter bits alternate between `fcr_ube` (active-high carry in, active-low carry out) and `fcr_ubo` (the opposite).
- The FFE DACs differ in size: main 4 bits, pre 2 bits, post 3 bits. The pre and post pairs are cross-wired (negative taps). The main pair is m=8, post m=4 and pre m=2.
- The PI tails are complementary: A has a fixed unit plus `wb`-legs, B has `w`-legs only.
- `fca_cmla` uses `rl=600` in the lanes and `rl=450` in the clock lane. `fca_mix2w` uses `rl=420` instead of its default of 500.
- The Tx uses DLL phase `ph[0]` directly as its bit clock.
- The vote samples 3 of 8 PD decisions per word. This decimation is a design choice.

## 6. Unused outputs and intended stubs

- Flat level: no floating nets and no gate-only (undriven) nets.
- Per cell, there are 51 single-connection nets. All are deliberately unused outputs and are listed in `scripts/intended_stubs.json`:
  - Flop `qb` outputs:
    - `fcr_bbx`: s0b, s1b, e0b, e1b
    - `fcr_vote`: u1b, u2b, d1b, d2b
    - `fcr_dsr8`: srb[7:2]
    - `fcx_ser8`: sqb[7:0]
    - `fcx_ffe`: d1b, d2b
    - `fcs_creg`: cqb[3:0]
    - `fcr_jdiv8`: q0b, q2b
  - `fca_dll`: up, dnb (the PFD outputs the pump does not use).
  - `fca_dline`: dmp, dmn (dummy cell).
  - `fcr_acc`: cb2, cb3, cb4, cub5, cdb5.
  - `fct_mon`: dq[1:0], dqb[2:0], cb[1:0], cb[5:3].
  - `fcx_ser8`: sob.
  - `fcx_lane`: wckb.
- `cmd_q[3]` drives nothing inside; it is read back only.

## 7. Look-alike traps

| # | Block | Looks like | Really is | How the netlist tells them apart |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `fca_mix2w` (in `fcr_phmix`) | Summer / FFE (it is wired like `fcx_drv`) | Phase interpolator | <ul><li>The pair inputs are two adjacent DLL clock phases, coming through `fcr_phsel` from `ph[7:0]`. They are not delayed copies of one data stream.</li><li>The tail weights are complementary (A = 1 + legs on `wb`, B = legs on `w`), so the total is always 4 units.</li><li>The weights come from the CDR accumulator `code`/`codeb`, not from register ports.</li><li>The loads carry slew caps C0/C1.</li><li>The output goes to the sampler clock pins and to `fca_c2c`, not to a pad.</li><li>No pair is cross-wired for a negative tap.</li></ul> |
| 2 | `fca_isw` | Tri-state or current-starved inverter | DLL charge pump | <ul><li>The inner gates are two different signals: `upb` from the PFD UP flop's qb, and `dn` from the DN flop's q.</li><li>The outer gates are bias nodes: `vbp` from the diode MP0, and `ib` from the diode MN0 that `ib_cp` feeds.</li><li>The output `vctl` is an analog node. It goes to the R+C filter (`fca_lpf`), the MOS decap MN1, and three sets of bias/starve gates: the delay-line NMOS starve devices, the vcp converter MN0, and, at the top, the RO replica. It also goes to the 20 k monitor. It never drives a logic input.</li></ul> |
| 3 | `fct_cs5` | Buffer chain of starved inverters | 5-stage ring oscillator | <ul><li>The last node `r4` returns to the gate of the first (NAND) stage: MN1.g / MP1.g. The chain is closed.</li><li>There are 5 inverting stages, an odd number.</li><li>The only other input is the enable `en`. When `en = 0`, MP2 forces `r0` high and the ring holds the static pattern 1,0,1,0,1.</li><li>The switch-level sim never settles with `en = 1`.</li></ul> |
| 4 | `fcs_inrx` Schmitt (MP0/MP1/MN1/MN2 + MP2/MN3) | Latch, because the output feeds back | Schmitt trigger | <ul><li>A single input `pi` drives all four stack gates.</li><li>The feedback devices take the gate `sx` (the output). One channel terminal sits on a stack midpoint (`p1` or `n1`, the d pin) and the other goes to the opposite rail (MP2 to vssq, MN3 to vddq).</li><li>There is no cross-coupled inverter pair, no clock and no second data input.</li><li>The output follows the input.</li></ul> |
| 5 | `fcr_bbx` | BIST/PRBS checker or a plain sampler bank (DFFs + XORs) | Alexander bang-bang PD | <ul><li>The inputs are a data sample and an edge sample of the same signal, half a UI apart.</li><li>The flops use both clock edges: X0, X1 and X3 have ck/ckb swapped.</li><li>Each XOR compares an edge sample with a neighbouring data bit.</li><li>There is no LFSR, no pattern generator and no error counter.</li><li>The outputs go to `fcr_vote` → `fcr_acc` → PI code, which is a loop.</li><li>The data flops are also the first deserializer stages.</li></ul> |
| 6 | `fca_dcell` / `fca_dline` | Static slew-limited inverters with fixed starve bias | Voltage-controlled delay line of a DLL | <ul><li>The starve gates `vcn`/`vcp` are `vctl` (charge pump + loop filter) and its PMOS mirror `vcp`, not fixed bias.</li><li>The chain's tap `ph[0]` returns to the PFD `fb` input.</li><li>The weak cross-coupled pair (L = lcs, W = wkn/wkp) only keeps the two outputs complementary. It is not a latch: there is no clock, and the starved drivers overpower it.</li></ul> |

Extra traps (documented in the key):
- **`fce_clmp`/`fce_clmphv`:** a three-inverter chain driving a big NMOS between the rails. It looks like a buffer chain, but it is an RC-triggered ESD clamp. Its input is the R–C node, and it is off in steady state.
- **`fcr_jdiv8`:** four flops in a row, like the deser shift register, but closed with inverted feedback (`wckb` → `X0.d`). It is a ÷8 divider plus a pulse decode.
- **`fca_pfd`:** reset flops again, but D is tied to vddd and the outputs reset themselves through NAND → delay → `rb`. It is a PFD, not a sampler and not the Alexander PD.
- **`fcr_phsel`:** TG mux trees like a serializer, but they select a static clock phase and change only when the code steps.
- **`fca_cl`:** contains a cross-coupled pair, but that is the CML latch's regeneration half. The clock steers the tail between the track pair and the regeneration pair.
- **`fca_phd`:** a single inverter per phase looks like it inverts the phases, but the index rotation by 4 restores them.

## 8. Checks (`scripts/run_all.sh`)
`````

`````json
   "notes": "Feedback loops: (1) DFE decision loop RXD[3] -> X_PH0 select -> RXD[0] -> X_PH1 -> ... -> RXD[3], one phase per UI (critical timing loop); (2) offset-cal loop: phase-0 decision complement DB0 -> counter UP -> trim DAC -> M_TN/M_TP in all 8 comparators -> decisions. Only phase 0 is observed and all 8 comparators share one trim code (common-offset cancellation, dominated by the CTLE): intentional asymmetry. In cal mode the tap DAC is forced off (alpha = 0), so H and L comparators are equivalent. RXD[3:0] are staggered by one UI each; all four are stable together for one UI around the next PH[0] rising edge (RXCLK). Main path PADR -> RXD non-inverting."
  },

   "controls": {
    "START": "command: one ZQ_CLK-cycle pulse starts a calibration (and clears all state)",
    "KEEPB": "comparator decision, active low: 0 = keep the trial bit"
   },
   "notes": "MSB first, one bit per ZQ_CLK; DONE rises on the 5th clock after the START clock and holds until the next START; BUSY (= NOT DONE) is high exactly while a token is in flight. No reset pin: everything is cleared synchronously by START, so the code is undefined until the first calibration. Dynamic flops: ZQ_CLK must be free-running so the hold muxes refresh the code every cycle. Q of X_C4..X_C0 and QB of X_FD are unused (CODE is built from QB). Multi-output."
  },

   "role": "LPDDR5-style x8 DQ byte IO (memory side): 8 bidirectional DQ slices (4:1 serializer with FFE post lane, slew-coded predriver, LVSTL NMOS-NMOS driver, pull-down ODT; CTLE + 4-phase loop-unrolled DFE with double-tail comparators and offset calibration), WCK CML input with in-path DCA, analog DCC and /2 I/Q generation, quarter-rate phase tree, R-2R VREF, DFE tap DAC, ZQ 5-bit SAR, control decode, bias and ESD",
   "on_high_speed_path": true,
   "inverting": null,
`````
