### FILE: tests/regression/t4_lpddr5/answer_key_README.md
<!-- sha256=f89c3376e7951d201b03c6840ad52d2b005862c7d49bbff24093ab70c2d29217 newline=1 -->
`````markdown
# Answer key format

`netlist_f.json` is the designer's ground truth for `netlist_f.sp`, an LPDDR5-style x8 DQ byte IO (memory side). Its top cell is `LP5_DQ_BYTE`. The format and the class vocabulary are the same as the iter3 key (`nand_io_full.json`). Only the bus and instance notation changes, because this netlist uses bracket buses and individually written instances. No new classes are needed.

## Top-level fields

- `netlist`: the netlist file.
- `top`: the top cell. It is a `.subckt`, and nothing instantiates it.
- `supplies`, `grounds`: the supply and ground port names.
  - `VDD` is the core supply (about 0.75 V); `VDDQ` is the LVSTL IO supply (about 0.5 V).
  - The grounds are `VSS` (core) and `VSSQ` (IO).
- `ports`: one entry per top-cell port or bus. A bus is written `NAME[MSB:LSB]`. The 114 pins are grouped into 32 entries. Each entry has:
  - `class`: one of the port classes below.
  - `function`: a one-line description.
- `cells`: one entry for **every** subcircuit in the netlist (49). That covers hierarchical cells and leaf cells, whether or not they are on the high-speed path.

## Port classes

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `hs_data_in` / `hs_data_out` / `hs_data_io` | High-speed (bit-rate) data. `DQ[7:0]` is `hs_data_io` because the pad is bidirectional. |
| `clock_in` / `clock_out` | Clocks. `WCK`/`WCKB` are the high-speed write clock. `TXCLK`/`RXCLK` are quarter-rate word clocks to the core. `ZQ_CLK` is a slow calibration clock; its function text says so. |
| `word_rate_data` | Core-side parallel data: `TXD[31:0]` (serializer inputs) and `RXD[31:0]` (DFE decisions, one bit per UI per DQ). |
| `important_control` | Controls that change the high-speed behaviour in mission mode: enables, strengths, equalization, slew, threshold, termination, and mode switches (`OE`, `EQ_EN`, `SR`, `ODT_*`, `VREF_CODE`, `CTLE_CODE`, `DFE_TAP`, `RX_EN`, `CK_EN`, `DCC_EN`, `CAL_EN`). |
| `general_control` | Resets and settings that only initialize or restart something and leave the steady-state high-speed path unchanged (`DIV_RST`, `DCC_RST`). |
| `command` | A strobe that starts an operation: `ZQ_START`. |
| `status_out` | Read-back and status: `ZQ_DONE`, `ZQ_CODE[4:0]`, `CAL_DONE`. |
| `test_digital` | Defined for completeness; not used. |
| `reference` | Reference voltage or resistor pins: `ZQ`. |
| `bias` | Bias current: `IBIAS`. |
| `power` | Supplies and grounds. |
| `slow_signal` | Defined for completeness; not used at the top. |

Controls are classed by their effect, not by their name.
- `SR[1:0]` (slew) sets the output edge rate, so it is `important_control`.
- `DCC_EN` decides whether the clock duty is corrected, so it is `important_control`.
- `CAL_EN` disconnects the receiver input and forces the DFE tap to zero, so it is `important_control`.
- `DCC_RST` and `DIV_RST` only restart a loop or align a phase, so they are `general_control`.

## Per-cell fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `role` | What the block is. |
| `on_high_speed_path` | `true` if the cell carries the high-speed data or clock in series: the Tx data path (serializer, predriver, legs), the Rx data path (CTLE, comparators, DFE mux-latch), the WCK clock path (pad series R, CML buffer, CML-to-CMOS, DCA, divider, tree), and the slices and top that contain them. Static control, bias, calibration (DCC detector/OTA, ZQ, offset-cal counter/DAC/timer), termination, VREF and ESD shunt cells are `false`. A generic library cell is `true` if any instance of it sits on such a path. |
| `inverting` | Polarity from the main input to the main output. It is `null` for cells with several outputs or functions, or with no single in-to-out path. For multi-output cells that still have a clear main output (for example `DFF_TSPC`, `TX_PDRV`, `TX_SER4`), the value refers to the main output and `notes` explains the others. |
| `children` | Subcircuit instances only, one entry per instance (this netlist has no iterated instances). MOS, R and C devices are not listed. |
| `signal_flow` | A list of `[source, destination, net, net_class]` entries. It gives the main paths and is not an exhaustive connectivity dump. Bidirectional pads appear in both directions. |
| `controls` | Maps a control net (or bus `[MSB:LSB]`) of the cell to what it sets. |
| `notes` | Feedback loops, unused outputs, intentional asymmetry, cross-wiring and so on. |

## `signal_flow` endpoint syntax

- `PORT.<pin>` is a pin of the cell itself.
- `<inst>.<pin>` is a pin of a child instance, using the pin name from that child's `.SUBCKT` line.
  - A bus pin range is allowed: `X_SER.TXD[3:0]`. Its net is a bus of the same width, matched bit by bit, MSB first.
  - `X_DQ1.TXD[3:0]` with net `TXD[7:4]` means `X_DQ1.TXD[3]` is on `TXD[7]`, and so on.
- `<MOS>.<d|g|s|b>` is a MOS terminal.
- A bare device name (`R_SEC`, `C_INT`) is a passive R or C; the terminal does not matter, but the device must touch the named net.
- Net names follow the netlist.
  - Buses use `[MSB:LSB]`.
  - A stepped range `[start:stop:step]` is accepted by the checker but not used.

## `net_class` values

`net_class` is the direction-free form of the port classes:
- `hs_data`
- `clock`
- `word_rate_data`
- `important_control`
- `general_control`
- `command`
- `status`
- `reference` (VREF nodes, ladder nodes, ZQ pad and divider, CTLE VREF input)
- `bias` (bias voltages, including the code-set DAC outputs `VALF`, `VTRN`, `VTRP`)
- `slow_signal` (loop-internal nodes: DCC detector outputs and `VCTRL`, counter and SAR internals, comparator decisions inside calibration loops)
- `test_digital`
- `power`

## Conventions

- Buses are written MSB first.
- In a DQ slice, `TXD[0]` / `RXD[0]` (top-level `TXD[4n]` / `RXD[4n]`) is the first UI of the 4-UI word.
- Instance multiplicity (`M=` on an X line) gives leg weights. It is shown in the netlist and mentioned in `role` or `children`. The flattened MOS count (3973) counts device instances and ignores `M`.

## Checks run on this file (`scripts/check_key.py`)

- The `ports` entries expand to exactly the 114 pins of `LP5_DQ_BYTE`, and every class is from the list above.
- The key's top is the netlist's only uninstantiated cell.
- Every subcircuit has an entry, and every entry names a subcircuit; every entry has all seven fields, and `role`/`notes` are non-empty.
- Every child list matches the netlist exactly (instance name and cell), with a role per child.
- Every endpoint names an existing pin, instance, MOS terminal or passive device.
- Every net exists in its cell.
- Every endpoint, scalar or range, really connects to the net named for it (bit by bit for ranges).
- Every `controls` key is a net of the cell.
`````

### FILE: tests/regression/t4_lpddr5/intent.md
<!-- sha256=cebf20ae22bdd37f46d12c6244348773dcfd448cd30154584f30cd6e9030eac7 newline=1 -->
`````markdown
# LPDDR5-style x8 DQ byte IO: designer's note (verifier only)

`netlist_f.sp` is an `hspiceD`-style export of one top cell, **`LP5_DQ_BYTE`**: the memory-side IO of one LPDDR5-style byte (8 DQ pins, WCK/WCKB, ZQ). It is self-contained, with placeholder `.MODEL` cards and no `.include`. The top cell is a `.SUBCKT` that nothing instantiates.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Subcircuits | 49 (libraries LP5IO_STD 7, TX 9, ODT 3, RX 8, REF 2, CLK 10, CAL 5, ESD 3, TOP 2) |
| Hierarchy depth | 5 levels, for example `LP5_DQ_BYTE / DQ_SLICE / RX_DQ / RX_PHASE / DT_CMP` |
| Cells mixing devices and instances | 12: `TX_PDRV`, `RX_DQ`, `TAP_DAC`, `VREF_R2R`, `CML2CMOS`, `DIV2_IQ`, `DCC_LOOP`, `CLK_TREE`, `ZQ_CAL`, `PAD_IN`, `DQ_SLICE`, `LP5_DQ_BYTE` |
| Flattened MOS | 3973 (NCH 842, NCH_LVT 1572, PCH 424, PCH_LVT 1107, NCH_IO 15, PCH_IO 13) |
| Flattened R / C | 219 / 57 |
| Device lines in the file | 195 X, 220 M, 38 R, 21 C |
| Top pins | 114 |

## Conventions

**Supplies:**
- `VDD` is the core supply, about 0.75 V. It feeds the logic, the clock path, the predrivers and the receiver.
- `VDDQ` is the LVSTL IO supply, about 0.5 V. It feeds the driver pull-ups, the ZQ divider and the VREF ladder.
- `VSS` is the core ground. `VSSQ` is the IO ground, used by the driver pull-downs, ODT, the ZQ replica and ESD.
- Every NMOS bulk is on `VSS`/`VSSQ` and every PMOS bulk on `VDD`/`VDDQ`. A device whose source or drain touches an IO rail has its bulk on the IO rail. For example, the pull-up NMOS has its drain on `VDDQ` and its bulk on `VSSQ`.

**Devices:**
- `NCH`/`PCH` are core devices; `NCH_LVT`/`PCH_LVT` are low-Vt devices for the HS data and clock cells.
- `NCH_IO`/`PCH_IO` are thick-oxide devices, used only in ESD.
- The LVSTL driver, ODT and ZQ replica use thin `NCH`, because VDDQ is about 0.5 V.

**Naming:**
- Cells are uppercase.
- Instances have descriptive names (`X_SER`, `X_PH0`, `X_DQ3`). MOS devices are `M_*`, resistors `R_*`, capacitors `C_*`.
- Buses are `NAME[n]`, MSB first, and every repeated instance is written out individually.
- Leg weights are instance multipliers `M=` on X lines.

**Comments:** only the export header and the `Library name` / `Cell name` / `View name` / `End of subcircuit definition.` lines.

## Top-level pins

| Pin | Class | Function |
|---|---|---|
| `DQ[7:0]` | hs_data_io | Bidirectional data pads. Write data goes in to the CTLE and DFE receiver; read data goes out from the LVSTL driver with de-emphasis. |
| `WCK`, `WCKB` | clock_in | Differential write clock at half the data rate. Its ÷2 gives four quarter-rate phases that clock both Tx and Rx. |
| `ZQ` | reference | Pad to the external RZQ, which goes to VDDQ. |
| `TXD[31:0]` | word_rate_data | Core read data. `TXD[4n+k]` is DQ n, UI k. It is launched on `TXCLK` rising. |
| `RXD[31:0]` | word_rate_data | Receive decisions. `RXD[4n+k]` is DQ n, UI k. The four bits are staggered by one UI and are all stable around `RXCLK` rising. |
| `TXCLK`, `RXCLK` | clock_out | Quarter-rate word clocks: buffered left-spine phase 2 and phase 0. |
| `OE` | important_control | Driver enable. 0 turns all legs off (Hi-Z); 1 also forces ODT off. |
| `EQ_EN` | important_control | De-emphasis (post-cursor segment) enable. |
| `SR[1:0]` | important_control | Main-segment predriver slew code. |
| `ODT_EN`, `ODT_CODE[2:0]` | important_control | Pull-down ODT enable and strength. |
| `VREF_CODE[3:0]` | important_control | Receiver threshold: VDDQ/2 × code/16. |
| `CTLE_CODE[1:0]` | important_control | CTLE peaking. |
| `DFE_TAP[2:0]` | important_control | DFE h1 magnitude α. 0 turns the DFE off. |
| `RX_EN` | important_control | Rx PMOS bias and the VREF ladder. |
| `CAL_EN` | important_control | Rx offset-cal mode. |
| `CAL_DONE` | status_out | Offset calibration finished. |
| `ZQ_CLK` | clock_in | Slow, free-running ZQ clock. |
| `ZQ_START` | command | One-cycle pulse that starts a ZQ calibration. |
| `ZQ_DONE` | status_out | ZQ calibration finished. |
| `ZQ_CODE[4:0]` | status_out | ZQ code readback. The same nets drive the Tx legs. |
| `CK_EN` | important_control | WCK receiver enable. |
| `DCC_EN` | important_control | Duty loop on. When 0, VCTRL is held at its preset. |
| `DCC_RST` | general_control | Forces VCTRL to its preset. |
| `DIV_RST` | general_control | ÷2 I/Q reset. |
| `IBIAS` | bias | Reference current. |
| `VDD`, `VSS`, `VDDQ`, `VSSQ` | power | Supplies and grounds. |

## Block list and signal flow

### Clock: WCK to the quarter-rate phases (`X_CKGEN` = `CLK_GEN`, `X_CKTREE` = `CLK_TREE`)

1. `WCK`/`WCKB` enter through `PAD_IN`: dual-diode ESD plus a 100 Ω secondary series R.
2. `CML_BUF` is a PMOS-input CML stage (the inputs sit at low common mode) with 600 Ω loads to VSS. Its tail is enabled by `CK_EN`.
3. `CML2CMOS` is an NMOS 5T differential-to-single-ended amplifier followed by `INV_D1` and `INV_D4`. Its output is `CKC`.
4. `DCA_CS` is the in-path, current-starved duty adjuster, giving `CKA`.
   - Only the pull-down of its first inverter is starved, by `M_NS` (gate `VCTRL`).
   - `M_NM`, with its gate tied to VDD, keeps a minimum current.
5. `DIV2_IQ` is the ÷2 quadrature generator: two `DLAT_D` latches in a ring.
   - `X_L1` is transparent on CK high and `X_L2` on CK low.
   - The ring inverts in its wiring (`X_L1.D` = `PH[3]`, which is `X_L2.QB`).
   - Outputs: `PH[0]` = I, `PH[1]` = Q, `PH[2]` = IB, `PH[3]` = QB. `PH[k]` is high during 90° steps k and k+1.
6. `CLK_TREE` distributes the four phases.
   - Each phase has a two-inverter root, then one **inverting** `INV_D4` spine driver per side with 30 Ω / 20 fF wire RC.
   - The left spine `PHL` serves DQ0–3; the right spine `PHR` serves DQ4–7.
   - Because the spine drivers invert, `PHL[(k+2)%4]` is driven from `PH[k]`.
7. Spine taps: `PHL[2]` goes to `TXCLK` (two `INV_D4`) and to the cal clock; `PHL[0]` goes to `RXCLK`.

### DCC, analog (`DCC_LOOP` inside `CLK_GEN`)

- `DCC_DET` senses `CKA`, the full-rate CMOS clock, with a phase splitter.
  - The true side is two inverters; the complement side is one inverter plus an always-on TG for delay matching.
  - Each side feeds a 100 kΩ / 1 pF low-pass filter, with 0.5 pF across `VP`/`VN`.
  - VP ≈ D·VDD and VN ≈ (1−D)·VDD, where D is the duty cycle.
- `DCC_OTA` is a 5T Gm stage that integrates onto `C_INT`; that node is `VCTRL`.
  - Its inputs are **crossed**: `VN` goes to INP and `VP` to INN.
  - So a duty above 50 % lowers VCTRL, which slows the DCA rising edge and lowers the duty: negative feedback.
- A TG forces VCTRL to `VPRE` (0.6·VDD, from a resistor divider) when `DCC_RST`=1 or `DCC_EN`=0.
- There is no digital code.
- The DCC corrects the full-rate clock because the ÷2 outputs are 50 % by construction. What depends on the input duty is their I/Q spacing.

### Tx, per DQ (`TX_DQ` = `TX_SER4` → `TX_PDRV` → `TX_DRV`)

**4:1 serializer (`TX_SER4`):**
- The core launches `TXD[3:0]` on `PH[2]`, which is `TXCLK`.
- Bits are captured on staggered phases. `X_FF0` and `X_FF1` both capture on `PH[3]`, `X_FF2` on `PH[0]` and `X_FF3` on `PH[1]`. All four flops are TSPC (`DFF_TSPC`).
- `SER_MUX4` shows bit k in window k = `PH[k]`·`PH[k+3]`.
  - It is built from four 3-high clocked inverters on one node, so it **inverts**.
  - The main mux `X_MUXM` is therefore fed the flops' QB, which makes `DS` non-inverting.

**FFE post-cursor (in `TX_SER4`):**
- A second `SER_MUX4`, `X_MUXP`, is fed the flops' **Q**, rotated by one lane. `D[k]` = bit k−1, and `D[0]` = bit 3 of the previous word, which `X_FF3` still holds.
- Its output `PS` = ~bit(k−1), the "1-UI-delayed inverted data". There is no delay flop: the rotation is the delay.

**Predriver (`TX_PDRV`):**
- Main segment: `PUG_M` = `SLEW_INV`(~DS) = DS and `PDG_M` = `SLEW_INV`(DS) = ~DS.
- `SLEW_INV` has a base leg plus x1/x2 legs enabled by the static `SR[1:0]`/`SRB[1:0]` code.
- Post segment: plain inverters give `PDG_P` = ~PS and `PUG_P` = PS.

**Driver legs (`TX_DRV`):**
- Main: 5 binary `TX_LEG_M` legs, M = 16/8/4/2/1.
- Post: 3 `TX_LEG_P` legs, M = 16/8/4. A post leg is a 1/4-size unit.
- A leg is an NMOS–NMOS LVSTL leg.
  - Pull-up: `VDDQ` → enable NMOS → data NMOS (**source follower, non-inverting from gate to pad**) → 300 Ω → pad.
  - Pull-down: pad → 300 Ω → data NMOS → enable NMOS → `VSSQ`.

**Segment enables (`TX_CTRL`, shared by the byte):**
- `EN_M[4:0]` = `ZQ_CODE` AND `OE`.
- `EN_P[2:0]` = `EN_M[4:2]` AND `EQ_EN`.
- They gate the stacked enable devices of the legs. The predriver itself has no enable.

### ODT, per DQ (`ODT_PD`, decode `ODT_CTRL`)

- Pull-down only, to VSSQ: 3 `ODT_LEG` legs (600 Ω + NMOS), M = 4/2/1.
- `ODT_G[k]` = `ODT_CODE[k]` AND `ODT_EN` AND NOT `OE`.

### Pad, per DQ (`DQ_SLICE`)

- `ESD_DIO2`: gate-tied PCH_IO to VDDQ and NCH_IO to VSSQ.
- `C_PAD`.
- ODT and the Tx legs connect on the pad node, ahead of the 150 Ω secondary R `R_SEC`.
- The receiver connects after `R_SEC`, on `PADR`.

### Rx, per DQ (`RX_DQ`)

**Cal input mux:**
- `M_ISO` is a series NMOS from `PADR` to `RXIN`, on when `CAL_ENB`=1.
- `M_CSN`/`M_CSP` form a TG from `RXIN` to `VREF`, on in cal mode.

**VREF (`VREF_R2R`, shared):**
- A 4-bit voltage-mode R-2R ladder.
- `VTOP` = VDDQ/2 comes from a divider enabled by `RX_EN`.
- Each bit has an NMOS-only SPDT switch (VTOP or VSSQ) into its 2R leg.
- The output impedance is 1 kΩ at every code, with 2 pF of decoupling. VREF is distributed unbuffered.

**CTLE (`CTLE_SC`):**
- Pseudo-differential PMOS pair: `RXIN` against `VREF`.
- Two PMOS tails (`VBP`), 1.5 kΩ loads to VSS, and 800 Ω degeneration.
- A 2-bit statically switched series-cap bank sits across the sources (`CTLE_CODE`).
- `OUTP` is the drain of the VREF-side device.

**Loop-unrolled 1-tap DFE, 4 phases (`X_PH0..3` = `RX_PHASE`):**
- Phase k is clocked by `PH[k]`, with `CKB` = `PH[k+2]`.
- Each phase holds two `DT_CMP` double-tail comparators.
  - `X_CMPH` decides x > +α.
  - `X_CMPL` is the same cell with INP/INN, OUTP/OUTN and VTRN/VTRP all cross-wired, so its α device becomes −α.
- A `DFE_MUXLAT` picks H when the previous phase's decision is 1. It is a mux merged into a ratioed SR latch.
- Phase k's select is `RXD[k−1]`, and phase 0 uses `RXD[3]`.

**DFE α (`TAP_DAC`, shared):**
- A 3-bit PMOS current DAC into the NMOS diode `VALF`, which biases `M_AL` on each comparator's FP node.
- It is forced off when `CAL_ENB`=0.

**Offset calibration (per DQ):**
- In cal mode the CTLE input is shorted to VREF, the pad is isolated and α = 0.
- The phase-0 decision drives the counter: `DB0` → UP and `RXD[0]` → UPB of `RX_CAL_CNT`, a 3-bit saturating up/down counter.
- The counter feeds `RX_TRIM_DAC`. This 3-bit steering DAC makes `VTRN` ∝ code and `VTRP` ∝ 7−code, which bias `M_TN`/`M_TP` in all 8 comparators.

**Cal sequencing (`CAL_CTRL`, shared):**
- `PHL[2]` ÷4 gives `CAL_CK`, so the counters run synchronously with the decisions. A further ÷2 clocks a 5-stage shift-register timer of `CAL_EN`.
- `CAL_DONE` = S4·`CAL_EN`, about 9–10 `CAL_CK` edges after `CAL_EN`.
- `CAL_RUN` = `CAL_EN`·NOT `CAL_DONE` enables the counters.

**Bias (`BIAS_GEN`):** from `IBIAS` it makes:
- `VBP_B`, always on: CML buffer and ZQ comparator.
- `VBN`: CML2CMOS and DCC OTA.
- `VBP_A`, gated by `RX_EN`: CTLE, trim DACs and tap DAC.

### ZQ (`ZQ_CAL`)

- A VDDQ/2 divider, enabled by BUSY, gives `ZREF`.
- `ZQ_CMP` is a continuous-time two-stage comparator with a PMOS input pair. It compares the ZQ pad against `ZREF`. Its output `OUTB` is active-low "keep".
- `ZQ_SAR5`, a 5-bit SAR, works MSB first.
  - A one-hot token register is started by `ZQ_START`.
  - Each bit has a hold/decide TG mux, cleared synchronously by START.
  - CODE = C OR T. DONE is sticky, and BUSY = NOT DONE.
- 5 binary `ZQ_RLEG` replica pull-down legs (M = 16..1) sit on the pad. Each is a 1/6-scale copy of the `TX_LEG_M` pull-down half: R, then an "ON" NMOS gated by BUSY, then an enable NMOS gated by the code.
- A bit is kept while ZQ > VDDQ/2, meaning the pull-down is still too weak.
- `ZQ_CODE[4:0]` drives `TX_CTRL` (all main legs, and the post legs from bits 4:2) and is also a readback port.
- One code serves both pull-up and pull-down legs.

### ESD

- `ESD_DIO2` primary dual diodes on every pad: DQ, WCK, WCKB and ZQ.
- `ESD_CLAMP` RC-triggered rail clamps, one on VDDQ/VSSQ and one on VDD/VSS: 200 kΩ / 2 pF RC → inverter → 50 µm × 40 NMOS.
- Secondary series R: `R_SEC` 150 Ω in `DQ_SLICE` and 100 Ω in `PAD_IN`.
- Top-level decaps: `M_DCAP`, an NMOS, and `C_DCQ`.

## Timing summary (quarter-rate cycle = 4 UI, 90° per UI)

- **Tx launch and capture:**
  - The core launches TXD on `PH[2]`.
  - Captures: bit 0 and bit 1 on `PH[3]` (270°), bit 2 on `PH[0]` (360°), bit 3 on `PH[1]` (450°). Each is at least 90° inside the core window.
- **Tx mux windows:** bit k is shown at [360+90k, 450+90k].
- **Post lane hold:** the post lane's hold margin at the end of each window is one flop clock-to-Q. This is accepted: the window closes on the same edge that updates the flop.
- **Rx decisions:**
  - Phase k evaluates on `PH[k]` rising.
  - The phase-k decision must settle within one UI, because phase k+1 needs it as its select. This is the critical DFE loop timing.
- **RXD alignment:**
  - `RXD[k]` is valid from about 90k°+t to 90k°+360°+t.
  - All four bits are valid together in [270°+t, 360°+t]. `RXCLK` (phase 0) falls in that window when t is about 45°.

## Feedback loops

1. **DCC:** `CKA` → `DCC_DET` → `DCC_OTA` / `C_INT` (`VCTRL`) → `DCA_CS` → `CKA`. This is analog, continuous and negative, closed through the crossed OTA inputs.
2. **÷2 ring:** `X_L1` → `X_L2` → `X_L1`, with an inversion in the ring wiring.
3. **ZQ SAR:** CODE → replica legs → ZQ pad → `ZQ_CMP` → `ZQ_SAR5` → CODE. It is clocked by `ZQ_CLK`. The code path to the Tx legs is open loop at run time.
4. **DFE decision loop, per DQ:** `RXD[3]` → phase-0 select → `RXD[0]` → phase-1 select → … → `RXD[3]`. One phase per UI.
5. **Rx offset-cal loop, per DQ:** phase-0 decision → `RX_CAL_CNT` (UP = decision complement) → `RX_TRIM_DAC` → `M_TN`/`M_TP` in the comparators → decisions. It is active only while `CAL_RUN`=1.
6. **Local state:** the `DFE_MUXLAT` keepers, the `DLAT_D` keepers, and the comparator latches. In `CAL_CTRL`, `X_DV0..X_DV2` are T flops with D tied to their own QB.

## Intentional asymmetries

- **Tx capture phases** are uneven: bits 0 and 1 share `PH[3]`, then `PH[0]` and `PH[1]`. The post lane is the main lane rotated by one, and its D[0] is the previous word's bit 3.
- **Post segment:**
  - It has only 3 legs, on ZQ bits [4:2]. Its unit is 1/4 of the main unit, so the post/main strength ratio is about 7/31.
  - Its predriver has no slew control.
  - Total drive strength changes with `EQ_EN` (not compensated).
- **ZQ:** only a pull-down replica exists; the pull-up NMOS legs reuse the pull-down code. The replica is a 1/6-scale leg, so the drive is RZQ/6.
- **Offset cal:** only phase 0 is observed (its decision drives the counter), and all 8 comparators of a DQ share one trim code. The L comparators get the trim biases swapped so the correction has the same physical sign.
- **Clock taps:** DQ0–3 sit on the left spine, DQ4–7 on the right. `TXCLK`, `RXCLK` and the cal clock all tap the left spine (phases 2, 0 and 2).
- **DCC sensing:** it senses only the full-rate CMOS clock `CKA` (one phase plus a locally generated complement), not the four divided phases.
- **ODT** is pull-down only and is forced off by `OE`.

## Unused outputs, ties and intended single-connection nets

- `CAL_CTRL`: QB of `X_S0..X_S4` (nets `S0B..S4B`) is unused. The timer uses only Q.
- `ZQ_SAR5`: Q of `X_C4..X_C0` (nets `C4..C0`) is unused, because CODE and the hold mux use QB (`CB`). QB of `X_FD` (`DONEB`) is unused.
- The checker allows exactly these 11 per-cell nets. After flattening there are 0 single-connection nets and 0 gate-only (undriven) nets.
- Gates tied to rails, all on purpose:
  - `DCA_CS.M_NM`: gate at VDD, the minimum-current device.
  - `DCC_DET.M_GN`/`M_GP`: gates at VDD/VSS, an always-on delay-matching TG.
  - `ESD_DIO2`: gate-tied diodes.
  - Top `M_DCAP`: an NMOS decap.

## Look-alike traps

1. **Loop-unrolled DFE (`RX_PHASE`).** It looks like two samplers per phase (data plus edge, or a double sampler) followed by a serializer mux. Really, H and L are speculative comparators with thresholds ±α, and `DFE_MUXLAT` picks one using the previous phase's decision. `SEL`/`SELB` are data, not static controls.
2. **`X_CMPL` is not an inverted or complementary sampler.** It is the same `DT_CMP` with INP/INN, OUTP/OUTN and VTRN/VTRP cross-wired. Its single α device (on the cell's FP) therefore gives −α.
3. **`DFE_MUXLAT` is a 2:1 mux plus an SR latch in one ratioed cell.** Its set and reset AND-OR pull-down networks resemble a 4-input complex gate or a NAND-based SR latch.
4. **NMOS pull-up from VDDQ (`TX_LEG_M/P.M_PU`).** It is a source follower, non-inverting from gate to pad. So the PU gate carries true data (`PUG_M` = DS). It is not an inverting stage or an open-drain pull-down.
5. **Stacked `M_PUE`/`M_PDE` in the legs** look like the second input of a NAND/NOR stack. They are static strength and OE enables (`EN_M`/`EN_P`).
6. **ODT legs** (NMOS + R to VSSQ) look like a driver pull-down segment. They are static termination, with gates from `ODT_CTRL`.
7. **ZQ replica legs (`ZQ_RLEG`)** have the same topology as the driver pull-down. The "data" gate is BUSY and the enable gate is the code.
8. **`SER_MUX4`** (four 3-high clocked-inverter stacks on one node) looks like a 4-input NAND/NOR or a tri-state bus. It is a 4:1 phase-window mux, and it inverts.
9. **`X_MUXP`** looks like a duplicate or redundant serializer, for example for a strobe. It is the FFE post-cursor lane: the same flops' Q rotated by one bit, which gives 1-UI-delayed inverted data.
10. **`CLK_TREE`** looks like a matched buffer tree with straight indices. The spine drivers invert, so output index (k+2)%4 is driven from root k. Logically `PHL[j]` = `PH[j]`.
11. **`DIV2_IQ`**: two latches on complementary clocks look like a master-slave DFF. The ring inverts and both latch outputs are used, so it is a ÷2 Johnson I/Q generator.
12. **`DCA_CS`** looks like a VCDL or current-starved delay cell. Only one edge is starved, so it adjusts duty. `M_NM` (gate tied to VDD) is a minimum-current device, not a switch.
13. **`DCC_DET`**: the TG with gates on VDD/VSS is a delay-matching element. The RC filters sense duty and are not in series with the clock.
14. **`DCC_OTA` + `C_INT`** look like a buffer, regulator or comparator. They are a Gm-C integrator with crossed inputs; the output `VCTRL` is analog.
15. **`CML2CMOS`**: the 5T stage looks like a bias OTA but sits in series with the clock.
16. **`CTLE_SC`**: the "switched-capacitor" degeneration is a static code selecting caps (not clocked). `OUTP` is the drain of the VREF-side device.
17. **`RX_TRIM_DAC`** looks like a bias generator or current mirror. It is the offset-cal DAC. Its outputs feed small injection devices (`M_TN`/`M_TP`), and `TAP_DAC` feeds `M_AL`, inside each comparator; these look like extra input-pair devices.
18. **`VREF_R2R`**: each `M_H`/`M_L` pair looks like an NMOS-only inverter. It is an analog SPDT switch into a 2R leg.
19. **The cal input mux (`M_ISO` series NMOS plus the TG to VREF)** looks like ESD or a pass gate in the data path. `M_ISO` belongs to the cal mux.
20. **`RX_CAL_CNT`**: the TG muxes compute XNOR (`PJ` = C ? UP : UPB) and XOR (`DN` = C ? GB : G). The flop outputs are the selects, not the data. The counter's UP pin is the decision **complement** `DB0`.
21. **`ZQ_SAR5`**: the NAND2 on the two QBs is an OR (CODE = C | T). The comparator output is active-low (`KEEPB`).
22. **`CAL_CTRL`**: the 5-stage shift register is a timer for `CAL_DONE`, not a deserializer or delay line. The three T flops form a ripple divider.
23. **`BIAS_GEN.M_OFF`** is a PMOS from VDD onto `VBP_A`. It is the Rx power-down (sources off), not a startup device.

## Design limits and assumptions

- The TSPC flops are dynamic.
  - `ZQ_CLK` must be free-running so the SAR hold muxes refresh the code.
  - The Rx trim codes are refreshed by `CAL_CK`, which runs whenever WCK runs. After WCK has been stopped, rerun the offset calibration.
- The ZQ code drives the Tx legs live, including trial codes during calibration. So `ZQ_START` must be issued while the bus is idle.
- The ZQ code is undefined until the first `ZQ_START`. The offset-cal counters have no reset: a calibration resumes from the previous trim, and the window of about 9–10 `CAL_CK` edges covers the full 0..7 range.

## Checks (`scripts/`, run `run_all.sh`)

- `gen_netlist.py` writes the netlist from `gen_lib.py` and `cells_*.py`. `build_key.py` writes the key from `key_part1..3.py`.
- `check_netlist.py` covers:
  - parse, a single top, and define-before-use;
  - every subckt instantiated (except the top) and pin counts on all 195 instances;
  - models and W/L, and that every pin is used;
  - per-cell unused outputs against the intended list above;
  - flattened floating and gate-only nets;
  - bulk and rail rules;
  - statistics.
- `check_logic.py` holds 2132 switch-level checks of every digital cell:
  - gates, TG mux, TSPC flop, the 4:1 window mux, slew inverter and predriver;
  - `TX_CTRL`/`ODT_CTRL` (exhaustive), the serializer main and post lanes, and `TX_DQ` pad levels (full, main-dominant, weak, equal-strength de-emphasis, Hi-Z);
  - the double-tail comparator with rail inputs, `RX_PHASE`, `DFE_MUXLAT`, `DLAT_D` and the `DIV2_IQ` I/Q sequence;
  - `DCA_CS`, the `DCC_DET`/`DCC_LOOP` logic, `CLK_TREE` rotation and the `TAP_DAC`/`VREF_R2R` decode;
  - `RX_CAL_CNT` up/down/saturate/hold, plus an offset-cal loop against a behavioural comparator;
  - the `CAL_CTRL` ÷4 and timer;
  - `ZQ_SAR5` for all 32 targets, and `ZQ_CAL` gating;
  - a loop-unrolled DFE harness against a behavioural ±α comparator (0 errors with the DFE; errors with a fixed threshold).
- `check_top.py` holds 637 top-level switch-level checks. The analog front ends are bypassed by forcing nets.
  - All 8 DQ pads serialize `TXD` correctly through the rotating tree.
  - All 32 `RXD` bits capture the forced CTLE outputs.
  - `TXCLK`, `RXCLK` and the cal-clock phases are correct.
  - The strength codes reach the legs, ODT is interlocked with OE, the pads are terminated with OE=0, and `CAL_EN` gates the tap DAC.
- `check_key.py` is the answer-key consistency check.
- Not switch-level checked (analog): `CML_BUF`, `CML2CMOS` (5T), `CTLE_SC`, `DCC_OTA`, `ZQ_CMP`, `BIAS_GEN`, `RX_TRIM_DAC`, the ESD cells and the leg resistors. Their wiring and polarity are covered by the key and by the top-level check.
`````

    "weve": "powers VREF divider, comparators (via xhhhbx) and enables replica gates",
    "jitjma": "starts PU successive approximation",
    "al9b": "resets SAR (code 0) and PD counter (10000)"
   },
   "notes": "Two feedback loops. PU: SAR code -> gate driver -> replica PMOS legs into the ZQ pin against external RZQ -> comparator (kdzjl0=1 when ZQ > VREF, i.e. PU too strong) -> SAR clears the trial bit; 5 decisions after start, then wqqd4l. PD: counter code -> gate driver -> PD replica legs against an internal copy of the calibrated PU at v79w -> comparator (kdzjl0=1 when v79w > VREF, PD too weak) -> count up; runs continuously once wqqd4l (dithers +/-1 LSB). r19gn<4:0> and xydzi<4:0> gate-driver outputs are unused; the counter t1ehl9 input is tied to vss. Mjqc0jq is the PMOS diode receiving ici43i, giving the comparator tail bias. In udmp jxzrv is the shared slow calibration clock tvxkez; orzf/ebqty feed pk25sw (z0nj9x -> gugmik -> leg enables of all DQ/DQS drivers) and are also read back as mu0x/yxapm. Replica unit is 1/8 of the driver unit, so the calibrated code gives Rpu = RZQ/8 at the pad (37.5 ohm for RZQ = 300 ohm)."
  },

   "notes": "(woj6, ej5ebo) is valid for one DQS period after each yb1z edge. y3h4vh rise captures UI0/UI1 into jcjxgh/btk1; the next fj7kaj rise (one DQS period later) captures UI2/UI3 and re-registers jcjxgh/btk1, so y07ql<3:0> changes once per word (every 2 DQS periods) and the core can capture it on bodg (= y3h4vh) rising, mid-window. y07ql<0> is the first UI.     "c3ykk1": "resets the code to 10000 (neutral)",

   },
   "notes": "Closes the DCC loop through ne2krl: lze378 -> wtth -> RPT chain -> tree -> ehcfwv leaf -> qiex8 -> vui2 -> fn5wjn -> lze378. Duty > 50% -> t5n19 > op7f -> gidww=1 -> fwkdy counts gidww -> DCA PU legs shorten the high phase (negative feedback). Comparator evaluates on rz2bge rising, counter and lock detector update on rz2bge falling. After two valid dithers i7zg=1 drives hold. Comparator j1agx4 (rlip) unused. Switch-level check with a behavioural duty model: locks within +/-1 LSB from both sides and freezes. Not on the HS path (it only loads the sense leaf)."
  },

### FILE: tests/regression/t4_nameblind/answer_key_README.md
<!-- sha256=e01764bd29d2c7ef530f1dacd34b96861a1b8075682dbf216a34e3fc60745b9b newline=1 -->
`````markdown
# Answer key format

`nand_io_full.json` is the designer's ground truth for `nand_io_full.sp`, the full NAND flash IO block. Its top cell is `nf_io_top`. The format is the same as the sub-block keys in `material/answer_key`. The class vocabulary is extended as described below.

## Top-level fields

- `netlist`: the netlist file.
- `top`: the top cell. It is a `.subckt`, and nothing instantiates it.
- `supplies`, `grounds`: the supply and ground port names. They are `vdd`/`vccq` and `vss`/`vssq`.
- `ports`: one entry per top-cell port. A bus is written as `name<MSB:LSB>`; the 153 pins are grouped into 49 entries. Each entry has:
  - `class`: one of the port classes below.
  - `function`: a one-line description.
- `cells`: an entry for **every** subcircuit in the netlist (92). That covers all hierarchical cells and all leaf cells, whether or not they are on the high-speed path.

## Port classes

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `hs_data_in` / `hs_data_out` / `hs_data_io` | High-speed (bit-rate) data. `dq<7:0>` is `hs_data_io` because the pad is bidirectional. |
| `clock_in` / `clock_out` | Clocks and strobes. `dqs`/`dqsb` are bidirectional strobe pads and are classed `clock_in`; their function text says they are also driven on reads. `cal_clk` is a slow calibration clock. |
| `word_rate_data` | Core-side parallel data: `din<31:0>` (1:4 deser output) and `dout_e/o<7:0>` (serializer inputs). |
| `important_control` | Mode, enable and strength controls that change the high-speed behaviour (`rx_mode_um`, `dq_oe`, `odt_code`, ...). |
| `general_control` | Trims, resets and overrides (`dq_dskw`, `dqs_dly`, `sr_code`, `pu_ovr`, ...). |
| `command` | Command-decoder strobes that start an operation: `zq_start`, `dcc_train`. |
| `status_out` | Read-back and status: `zq_done`, `zq_pu_code`, `zq_pd_code`, `dcc_lock`, `dcc_code`. |
| `test_digital` | `tm_rxobs`, `rx_obs`. |
| `reference` | Reference voltage or resistor pins: `vref_ext`, `zq`. |
| `bias` | Bias current: `ibias`. |
| `power` | Supplies and grounds. |
| `slow_signal` | Defined for completeness; not used at the top. |

## Per-cell fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `role` | What the block is. |
| `on_high_speed_path` | `true` if the cell carries the high-speed data or clock/strobe signal in series: the mission data path, the strobe/clock distribution, the pad pass-through, the DCA in the RE path. Static control, bias, calibration (DCC detector/comparator/counter, ZQ), termination, test and rail-ESD cells are `false`. A generic library cell is `true` if any instance of it sits on such a path. |
| `inverting` | The polarity from the main input to the main output. It is `null` for cells with several outputs or several functions (for example the bidirectional slices), or with no single in→out path. |
| `children` | Subcircuit instances only. MOS, R and C devices are not listed. An iterated instance is listed once under its Virtuoso iterated name (`XI7<7:0>`), which stands for the expanded `XI7<7>` … `XI7<0>`. |
| `signal_flow` | A list of `[source, destination, net, net_class]` entries. It gives the main paths and is not an exhaustive connectivity dump. Bidirectional pads appear in both directions. |
| `controls` | Maps a control net (or bus `MSB:LSB`) to what it sets. |
| `notes` | Feedback loops, unused outputs, intentional asymmetry, mode muxes, and so on. |

## `signal_flow` endpoint syntax

- `PORT.<pin>` is a pin of the cell itself.
- `<inst>.<pin>` is a pin of a child instance, using the pin name from that child's `.subckt` line.
  - A range of an iterated instance is allowed (`XI7<7:0>.de`), including a stepped range (`XI0<14:0:2>.z`).
  - So is a bus pin (`XI7<7:0>.rd<3:0>`, whose net is the matching bus `din<31:0>`: `XI7<7>.rd<3>` maps to `din<31>`, …, `XI7<0>.rd<0>` maps to `din<0>`).
  - When a bus pin of an iterated range lists a narrower net (`XI7<7:0>.pu_en<4:0>` with `pu_en_d<4:0>`), every instance connects to that same bus.
- `<MOS>.<d|g|s|b>` is a MOS terminal.
- A bare device name (`RR0`, or an iterated group `RR1<30:0>`) is a passive R or C, or a ladder, where the terminal does not matter.
- Net names follow the netlist.
  - Buses use `<MSB:LSB>`.
  - A stepped range is `<start:stop:step>`, for example `t<31:1:2>` for the odd taps.

## `net_class` values

`net_class` is the direction-free form of the port classes. The values are:
- `hs_data`
- `clock`
- `word_rate_data`
- `important_control`
- `general_control`
- `command`
- `status`
- `reference` (VREF nodes, ladder taps, ZQ pin and replica nodes)
- `bias` (bias currents, self-bias and slew-bias nodes)
- `slow_signal` (loop-internal analog/digital nodes: detector outputs, comparator outputs, SAR phases)
- `test_digital`
- `power`

## Conventions

- Iterated instances and buses are written MSB first.
- In a bit slice, `rd<0>` / `din<4n>` is the first UI of the 4-UI word.
- Device multiplicity (`m=`) on subcircuit instances is shown in the netlist and mentioned in `role` and `notes`. The flattened MOS count (6833) counts device instances and ignores `m`; the sum of `m` is 7407.

## Checks run on this file (`scripts/check_key.py`)

- The `ports` entries expand to exactly the 153 pins of `nf_io_top`, and every class is from the list above.
- Every subcircuit has an entry, and every entry names a subcircuit.
- Every child list matches the netlist exactly, including iterated instances.
- Every endpoint names an existing instance or device and an existing pin.
- Every net exists in its cell.
- Every endpoint, scalar or range, really connects to the net named for it (bit by bit for ranges).
- Every `controls` key is a net of the cell.
`````

### FILE: tests/regression/t4_nameblind/intent.md
<!-- sha256=d656f865bd813f39eee3dad578a8b118c9cce7da499ded7f90680f4478f71728 newline=1 -->
`````markdown
# Name-blind copy of nand_io_full.sp (for the verifier only)

`netlist_e.sp` is the name-blind copy of `nand_io_full.sp` (iter3/agent1_full). It holds the same circuit, with every name replaced by a random token. RNG: Python `random.Random(583041)`, **seed 583041**. The top cell `nf_io_top` is now `udmp`.

- **Kept:** `vdd`, `vss`, `vccq`, `vssq`; every W/L/m/nf, R and C value; the `.TEMP` and `.OPTION` lines; the SPICE syntax; the comment shape.
- **Renamed:** subckts, models, libraries and views; instances (first letter kept, `<n>` kept); nets, pins and top ports (`<n>` kept). Nets are renamed per cell, so one old net name gets a different token in each cell.
- **Reordered:** the pin order of every `.subckt`, with every instance line permuted to match; the order of subckt definitions, device lines and model cards.
- **Files:** `name_map.json` holds the old-to-new map. `answer_key_e.json` is the answer key translated through it.
- **Checks:** the flattened connectivity maps back device for device. The key checker passes on the copy. No old name of 3 or more characters is in `netlist_e.sp`.

The designer's note below is unchanged and uses the original names. Translate them through `name_map.json`.

---

# NAND flash IO, full block: designer's note

`nand_io_full.sp` is a Virtuoso `hspiceD` export of one top cell, **`nf_io_top`**. It is the complete DDR (Toggle/ONFI-style) byte IO of a NAND die: 8 DQ pins, DQS/DQSB, RE/nRE, ZQ and VREF.

The file is self-contained. It has placeholder `.MODEL` cards and no `.include`. The top cell is itself a `.subckt`, and nothing instantiates it.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Subcircuits | 92 |
| Hierarchy depth | 6 levels (for example `nf_io_top` / `io_dq_slice` / `tx_dq_slice` / `tx_predrv` / `tx_predrv_leg` / `nand2_q`) |
| Cells mixing devices and instances | 22 (`rx_saff`, `tx_dca`, `tx_ser2`, `tx_predrv_leg`, `rx_vref_gen`, `zq_cal`, `io_pad_bidir`, ...) |
| Flattened MOS (instances) | 6833 (sum of `m=`: 7407) |
| Flattened R / C | 279 / 118 |
| Device lines in the file | 494 X, 292 M, 67 R, 36 C |

## Conventions

**Supplies:**
- `vdd` is the core supply, about 1.0 V. `vccq` is the IO supply, 1.2 V.
- The grounds are `vss` (core) and `vssq` (IO).
- `vss` and `vssq` are coupled only through the back-to-back ESD devices in `esd_rail`.

**Device flavours:**
- `nch`/`pch` are core devices.
- `nch_lvt`/`pch_lvt` are low-Vt core devices, used in the high-speed clock and data cells.
- `nch_hv`/`pch_hv` are thick-oxide IO devices. They are used everywhere on VCCQ and on every pad-facing gate.
- No core device touches `vccq`/`vssq`. Every NMOS bulk is on `vss`/`vssq` and every PMOS bulk on `vdd`/`vccq`; the structure check confirms both.

**Naming:**
- Instances are `XI<n>`. MOS devices are `MM<n>`, with a few named devices: `MMtail`, `MMclamp`, `MMN1`...
- Iterated instances are expanded MSB first (`XI7<7>` ... `XI7<0>`).
- Buses are MSB first (`code<4:0>`).
- Internal nets mix Virtuoso `net0xx` names with meaningful names.

**Libraries** (shown in the `** Library name:` comments):
- `NFIO_STD`: gates, flops, level shifters, clock buffers.
- `NFIO_RX`: receive path.
- `NFIO_TX`: transmit and RE clock path.
- `NFIO_CAL`: DCC and ZQ.
- `NFIO_ESD`: ESD.
- `NFIO_IO`: pad cells, ODT, control and bias hubs, slices, top.

## Top-level pins of `nf_io_top`

### High-speed pads (bidirectional, with ESD)

| Pin | Function |
|---|---|
| `dq<7:0>` | **High-speed data in/out.** Write data comes in to the Rx slices. Read data goes out from the Tx slices on the same pad. |
| `dqs`, `dqsb` | **Strobe, bidirectional.** On writes it is an input: a center-aligned strobe whose two edges sample DQ (`dqsb` is replaced by VREF in single-ended mode). On reads it is driven as an output strobe, generated from RE through a DQ-identical Tx slice, so it is edge-aligned to DQ. |
| `re`, `reb` | **Clock input**, RE/nRE (differential read enable; `reb` is replaced by VREF in single-ended mode). It is the read clock for all outputs. |

### Core-side data and clocks

| Pin | Function |
|---|---|
| `din<31:0>` | **Word-rate data out** to the core: 1:4 deserialized write data. `din<4n+3:4n>` holds DQ<n> UI3..UI0, so `din<4n>` is the first UI. All 4 bits of a word update together, once per DQS/2 period. |
| `din_clk` | **Clock out**: DQS/2 word clock (`div_p` buffered). The core captures `din` on its rising edge, which falls in the middle of the stable window. |
| `dout_e<7:0>`, `dout_o<7:0>` | **Word-rate data in** from the core: even and odd read data per DQ. The even bit is sent while the RE-derived clock is high, the odd bit while it is low. |
| `rclk_core` | **Clock out**: RE-derived clock (core tap of the Tx tree) that launches `dout_e`/`dout_o` and `dqs_burst`. |
| `cal_clk` | **Slow clock in** (about 10 MHz, from the core oscillator). It clocks the ZQ SAR and counter and the DCC comparator and counter. It is not a high-speed clock. |

### Reference and bias

| Pin | Function |
|---|---|
| `vref_ext` | Reference: external VREFQ pad (with ESD), used when `vref_int_en=0`. |
| `zq` | Reference: ZQ pad to the external RZQ, 300 Ω to VSSQ. Primary ESD only, with no series R. |
| `ibias` | Bias: about 10 µA from the bandgap. It is mirrored to the ZQ comparators (sink) and the VREF buffer (source). |

Internal reference and bias nets:
- `vref_rx` (VREFQ) is shared by the 8 DQ receivers, the single-ended DQS reference and the single-ended RE reference.
- `vref_zq` (VCCQ/2) is inside `zq_cal`.
- `vbp_sr`/`vbn_sr` are the pre-driver slew bias.
- `ib_zq` and `ib_vref` are the mirrored bias currents.

### Commands, status, test

| Pin | Class | Function |
|---|---|---|
| `zq_start` | command | One `cal_clk` pulse that starts the pull-up SAR (ZQ calibration command). |
| `dcc_train` | command | DCC training. 1 = run the duty loop while the host toggles RE. 0 = hold the code, clear the lock, gate off the detector and update clock. |
| `zq_done` | status out | Pull-up SAR finished. It also starts PD tracking. |
| `zq_pu_code<4:0>`, `zq_pd_code<4:0>` | status out | Read back the ZQ result. The same nets drive the driver strength internally. |
| `dcc_lock` | status out | DCC locked after two dither events. It also freezes the code. |
| `dcc_code<4:0>` | status out | Current DCC code (offset binary, 10000 neutral). |
| `tm_rxobs` / `rx_obs` | test | Observe `div_p` (DQS/2) on `rx_obs`. |

### Control codes and what they control

| Pin | Controls |
|---|---|
| `rx_en` | Rx power: DQ/DQS receivers (Bazes tails), strobe trees and chains, the VREF DAC qualifier, the observe gate. |
| `rx_mode_um` | **Rx path select.** 0 = matched: DQ goes through `dq_match_dly` and DQS through the 1→3→9 H-trees. 1 = unmatched: DQ goes direct and DQS through the 9-stage repeater chain, whose tap *n* drives DQ<n>. The inactive network is clock-gated (`en_m`/`en_u`; `selub` gates the DQ replica). |
| `dqs_se` | Single-ended DQS (DQS vs VREF) vs differential DQS/DQSB. |
| `vref_int_en` | Internal VREF DAC (ladder + OTA, powered only when selected) vs `vref_ext`. |
| `vref_code<4:0>` | Internal VREF tap, about 34.5 %…71.4 % of VCCQ in about 1.2 % steps. |
| `dqs_dly<2:0>` | Cap-load delay trim on both Rx strobe phases. |
| `dq_dskw<23:0>` | Per-bit Rx DQ deskew, 3 bits per bit (`dq_dskw<3n+2:3n>` for DQ<n>), for training in unmatched mode. |
| `rx_rst_n` | Resets the DQS/2 divider. The release point sets the deser word alignment. |
| `tx_en` | RE receiver enable. |
| `re_se` | Single-ended RE vs differential RE/nRE. |
| `dq_oe` | DQ driver enable. 0 = every PU and PD leg off (Hi-Z). 1 also forces the DQ-group ODT off. |
| `dqs_oe` | DQS/DQSB driver enable (preamble to postamble). 1 also forces the DQS-group ODT off. |
| `dqs_burst` | 1 = DQS/DQSB toggle with RE. 0 = DQS low and DQSB high (preamble/postamble). It is retimed in the slices. |
| `sr_code<1:0>` | Output slew: starving current of the pre-driver final stages. |
| `odt_en`, `odt_code<2:0>` | Termination on DQ/DQS/DQSB: about 300/150/100/75/60/50/43 Ω Thevenin for codes 1..7. It is effective only while that pin group is not driving. |
| `zq_en`, `zq_rst_n` | ZQ analog enable (VREF divider, comparators, replica gates, PD tracking). The reset gives SAR code 0 and PD counter 10000. |
| `drv_ovr_en`, `pu_ovr<4:0>`, `pd_ovr<4:0>` | Driver strength source. 0 = ZQ codes, 1 = override codes (bring-up/test). |
| `dcc_rst_n` | Resets the DCC code to 10000. |

## Signal flow and sub-blocks

### Rx (write data in)

1. **Pad.** `dq<n>` → `io_dq_slice/XI0 io_pad_bidir`. This is GDPMOS/GGNMOS primary protection, then 200 Ω + GGNMOS secondary protection, giving `pad_rx`.
2. **Front end.** `rx_dq_slice`: always-on input TG `rx_tg_q` → `rx_amp_bz` (Bazes self-biased receiver on VCCQ, DQ vs `vref_rx`) → `rx_ls_dn` (VCCQ→VDD) → `dly_trim3` (deskew).
3. **Path select.** `dq_match_dly` (a replica of the strobe `ckgate` + root/branch/leaf `ckbuf`), then three `mux2_hs` cells select data, rise strobe and fall strobe for matched or unmatched mode.
4. **Sampling.** `rx_samp_pair` holds two StrongARM `rx_saff`: rise samples on the true strobe, fall samples on the complement strobe.
5. **Deserialization.** `rx_deser4`: the rise sample is retimed onto the fall strobe. UI0/UI1 are captured on `div_p`. UI2/UI3 are captured on `div_n` and UI0/UI1 re-registered on `div_n`, so the 4-bit word changes once per word.
6. **Strobe path.** `rx_dqs_path` takes `dqs_rx`/`dqsb_rx` from the two `io_dqs_slice` pad cells:
   - An always-on DQS TG, plus DQSB/VREF select TGs.
   - Two identical `rx_amp_bz` with swapped inputs make the true and complement strobes, with equal latency.
   - Then `rx_ls_dn`, `dly_trim3` and `ckgate`.
   - Then the matched `rx_dqs_tree` ×2 and the unmatched `rx_rpt_chain` ×2.
7. **Word clock.** `rx_ckdiv_slice`: a mode mux on leaf/tap 8 of the true strobe, then the `dffr_tg` toggle divider giving `div_p`/`div_n`, then the `din_clk` driver.

**Matching by construction:** the DQ pad cell, TG, receiver, level shifter, trim, clock gate, buffers and mux are the same cells as on the strobe side. In matched mode the strobe-to-data delay difference cancels.

### Tx (read data out)

1. **RE input.** RE/nRE pads (`io_pad_in`) → `re_clk_path`.
2. **Receiver.** `tx_re_rx`: TGs, Bazes receiver, a dummy swapped receiver for input-load symmetry, `rx_ls_dn`.
3. **Duty adjust.** `tx_ckbuf_dca`: `ckbuf` → **`tx_dca`** (the DCC actuator) → `ckbuf_x8`.
4. **Distribution.** `tx_rpt_chain` (4 repeaters + RC wire) → `tx_cktree`:
   - Root, 2 branches of 6 leaves each.
   - `lf<7:0>` go to the DQ slices, `lf<8>` to DQS, `lf<9>` to DQSB.
   - A core tap feeds `tx_rpt` → `rclk_core`.
   - **`lf_dcc` = `ck_dcc`** is the DCC sense leaf, beside the DQS leaves.
5. **Per pin `tx_dq_slice`:**
   - `ck_split` (ck/ckb).
   - `tx_ser2`: even and odd DFFs on ck falling, a half-cycle latch on the odd path, and a TG mux. ck high sends even, ck low sends odd.
   - `ls_up_hs` (VDD→VCCQ).
   - `tx_predrv`: 5 × `tx_predrv_leg` (NAND/NOR with enables, then a current-starved final stage) → `pg<4:0>`/`ng<4:0>`.
6. **Main driver.** The pad cell's `tx_out_drv`: 5 × `tx_drv_unit` with m = 16/8/4/2/1. Each unit is pch_hv 8 µm + 300 Ω up and nch_hv 4 µm + 300 Ω down.
7. **DQS/DQSB.** These use the same `tx_dq_slice` and `io_pad_bidir` (`io_dqs_slice`). The constant patterns from `tx_ctrl` are DQS e=`dqs_burst`, o=0 and DQSB e=~`dqs_burst`, o=1.

### DCC loop (closed, on the RE → repeater → driver clock path)

The loop runs: `dcc_code` → `tx_dca` → RPT chain → tree → `ck_dcc` → `dcc_ctrl`.

Inside `dcc_ctrl`:
- `dcc_det`: a gated clock and its complement drive matched 2-pole RC filters (50 k/0.5 p, 50 k/0.25 p), giving `vp`≈D·VDD and `vn`≈(1−D)·VDD.
- `sa_cmp`: StrongARM comparator on `upd_clk` = `cal_clk` & `dcc_train`.
- `updn_cnt5`: up/down counter, reset to 10000.
- `dcc_lock_det`.
- The counter output `dcc_code` feeds back to `tx_dca`.

**Polarity:** duty > 50 % → `up`=1 → code counts up → the DCA pull-up legs speed the falling output edge → shorter high phase.

**Code map:** 1xxxx shortens the high phase by `code<3:0>` units. 0xxxx lengthens it by `~code<3:0>` units. 10000 and 01111 are both neutral, so the code is monotonic with one duplicate step.

**Lock:** after two valid decision reversals (the first decision after training starts is ignored), `dcc_lock`=1 drives the counter `hold` and freezes the code.

### ZQ calibration (`zq_cal`) → driver strength

**Pull-up loop:**
- `zq_vref` gives VCCQ/2.
- `zq_pu_rep` holds the replica PU legs on the ZQ pin, against RZQ.
- `zq_cmp` (static comparator + `ls_dn`) feeds `zq_sar5`, a 5-step SAR. A comparator 1 means ZQ is above VREF, so the PU is too strong and the trial bit is cleared. The result is `pu_code`.

**Pull-down loop:**
- `zq_pd_rep` is an internal PU copy on top of the PD replica legs, at node `npd`.
- `zq_cmp` feeds `updn_cnt5`, which tracks after `zq_done` and dithers ±1 LSB. The result is `pd_code`.

**Scaling:** the replica unit is 1/8 of the driver unit (1 µm + 2.4 kΩ vs 8 µm + 300 Ω). Matching RZQ = 300 Ω therefore sets the drivers to about 37.5 Ω.

**Code path to the drivers:**
1. `zq_cal.pu_code/pd_code` → `io_ctrl/drv_code_mux` (ZQ or override).
2. → `tx_ctrl`: level shift, then gate with `dq_oe` (DQ group) and `dqs_oe` (DQS group). This gives `pu_en_d/s<4:0>` (active-high PU enables) and `pd_dis_d/s<4:0>` (active-high PD disables).
3. → the per-leg pre-drivers of every DQ and DQS/DQSB slice.

### ESD and ODT

- **`io_pad_bidir`** (DQ ×8, DQS, DQSB) contains:
  - `esd_io_pad`: primary GDPMOS/GGNMOS plus a 200 Ω/GGNMOS secondary on the receiver side.
  - The main driver.
  - `odt_leg_pin`: 3 binary center-tapped PU/PD pairs.
  - A 0.2 pF pad cap.
- **`io_pad_in`** (RE, nRE, VREF_EXT): `esd_io_pad` and a pad cap.
- **ZQ:** `esd_prim`, primary only.
- **`esd_rail`:** RC-triggered clamps VCCQ-VSSQ and VDD-VSS, and `esd_b2b` VSS-VSSQ.
- **`odt_ctrl`** (in `io_ctrl`) makes separate gate buses for the DQ group and the DQS group: `odt_en & ~dq_oe` and `odt_en & ~dqs_oe`. The termination therefore never fights the driver it shares a pad with.

### Control and bias hubs (static)

- **`io_ctrl`** = `rx_ctrl` + `drv_code_mux` + `tx_ctrl` + `odt_ctrl`. All inputs are VDD-domain register/command bits. The `_q` outputs and the leg/ODT gate buses are VCCQ.
- **`io_bias`** = `ib_dist` + `tx_sr_bias` + `rx_vref_gen` (32-tap ladder, `vref_mux32` TG tree, `vref_buf_ota`, ext/int `amux2_q`, decap).

## What is and is not on the high-speed path

**On the path (in series with data or strobe/clock):**
- Rx: pad cells (passive pass-through), `rx_dq_slice` and below, `rx_dqs_path`, `rx_dqs_tree`, `rx_rpt_chain`, `rx_ckdiv_slice`.
- Tx: `re_clk_path` and below (including `tx_dca`), `tx_dq_slice` and below, `tx_out_drv`.
- Shared library cells: the HS library cells, and `dffr_tg`/`nand2_x1`/`nor2_x1` inside the divider.

**Not on the path:**
- Control: `io_ctrl` (`rx_ctrl`, `tx_ctrl`, `odt_ctrl`, `drv_code_mux`, `mux2_x1`, `ls_up`, `inv_x2`, `tie_hilo`).
- Bias and reference: `io_bias` (`ib_dist`, `tx_sr_bias`, `rx_vref_gen`, `vref_mux32`, `vref_buf_ota`, `amux2_q`).
- Calibration: `zq_cal` and all its children, and `dcc_ctrl` (`dcc_det`, `sa_cmp`, `updn_cnt5`, `dcc_lock_det`; it only loads the sense leaf).
- Termination and rail ESD: `odt_leg_pin` (a shunt load), `esd_rail`, `esd_rc_clamp`, `esd_b2b`, `esd_prim`.
- Test: `rx_obs_buf`.

**Signal categories:**
- Word-rate digital: `din<31:0>`, `dout_e/o<7:0>`, and inside the cells `p0/p1/rd` of the deser and `de/do/qe/qo` of the serializer.
- Slow loop-internal signals: `vp/vn/up`, `cmp_pu/cmp_pd`, SAR phase.

## Intentional asymmetries and unused nets

- **Dummy loads (unused outputs):**
  - `ckc_m<8>` and `ckc_u<8>`: the complement-strobe leaf/tap 8.
  - `tx_re_rx/net011`: the dummy receiver output.
  - `dcc_det/net012`.
- **Unused flop `qb` outputs:** the sampler `qb`s (`rx_samp_pair/net07`, `net08`), `zq_sar5 phb/codeb/doneb`, `updn_cnt5 cqb/net012`, `dcc_lock_det/net010`, `net011`, and the DCC comparator `qb` (`dcc_ctrl/net011`).
- **Unused level-shifter complements:** in `tx_ctrl`, `odt_ctrl`, `tx_sr_bias` and `zq_gate_drv`.
- **Unused gate-driver outputs:** `zq_cal pu_g<4:0>` and `pd_gb<4:0>`.
- **Other asymmetries:**
  - The ratioed `ls_up_hs` has unequal rise/fall delays.
  - The DCA's rise/fall asymmetry is the correction mechanism.
  - The `div_n` buffer is one inverter later than `div_p`. This is tolerated, because the deser window is a full DQS period.
- **Tie-offs:**
  - `dcc_lock_det/XI2` has its D tied to `vdd` (a valid flag).
  - The ZQ PD counter `hold` is tied to `vss`.

## Integration changes vs. the separate sub-block netlists

- The main driver legs moved from `tx_dq_slice` into the shared pad cell. The pad cap moved from `tx_out_drv` to `io_pad_bidir`.
- The DCC now lives in the RE path: the standalone `dcc_dca` was dropped and `tx_dca` is used. The detector now senses tree leaf `lf_dcc`, which was the dummy leaf. The local monitor tap was removed. A lock detector was added.
- `rx_deser4` now has 6 flops, so all 4 output bits update together. In the old version half the word changed on the core capture edge.
- The ZQ replica legs were rescaled to 1/8 of the driver unit, so the calibrated code gives the right driver impedance.
- `ib_dist` now also sources the VREF buffer bias.
- ODT now has per-group auto-off.
- The SE RE reference is the shared `vref_rx`.
- `wire_rc` was split into `wire_rc_rx`/`wire_rc_tx` (different RC), and duplicate library cells were merged.

## Checks run (scripts in `scripts/`)

**`check_netlist.py`:** all 92 subckts are defined before use and used, there is exactly one top, and the pin counts match. MOS have 4 terminals, a known model and W/L. The bulk/domain rules hold. No pin is unconnected inside its cell. Every single-connection net is in the intentional list above.

**`check_logic.py`:** a unit-delay switch-level simulation (`swsim.py`) of the netlist's own transistors. It passed 994 checks:
- Every standard gate and level shifter.
- Every flop and latch.
- `tx_dca` decode and polarity for all 32 codes.
- Tree and chain polarity.
- The DQS-slice serializer through the pad: even/odd order, Hi-Z, partial strength, ODT.
- Samplers + 6-flop deser + divider, with words checked in UI order.
- `updn_cnt5`: count, saturate, hold, reset.
- `zq_sar5` with a behavioural comparator: all 32 targets in 5 steps.
- The closed DCC loop with a behavioural duty model: it locks within ±1 LSB from both sides, freezes, and releases on `dcc_train`=0.
- `io_ctrl` decode on random vectors.

**Not simulated:** the analog cells (Bazes receivers, OTA, ZQ comparators, ESD, RC detector) were checked by inspection only.

**`check_key.py`:** validates the answer key against the netlist.
`````
